headline: Taslima Nasreen backs UCC, says India, Bangladesh, Pakistan need it
full_text:
Taslima Nasreen backs UCC, says India, Bangladesh, Pakistan need it
Taslima Nasreen backed a Uniform Civil Code during her return visit to Kolkata. She said equal laws are essential for women's rights and defended free expression after a felicitation disruption.
Exiled Bangladeshi author Taslima Nasreen on Sunday strongly backed the implementation of a Uniform Civil Code in India, saying such a law was essential to remove discrimination, especially against women. She said Bangladesh and Pakistan also needed a Uniform Civil Code, and argued that there should be equal laws for everyone.
Speaking to reporters in Kolkata during her first visit to the city in nearly 19 years, Nasreen also expressed anguish over a disruption at her felicitation ceremony a day earlier, when poet Joy Goswami was forced to leave the stage amid objections from a section of the audience. She said the incident went against the principle of freedom of expression, which Kolkata had long stood for.
"I have been fighting for the UCC for the past 40 years. This is much needed in any civilised country. Bangladesh, Pakistan and India need a Uniform Civil Code. There should be equal laws for everyone. Women face a great deal of discrimination, and much of it can be removed through a UCC. It is essential," Nasreen said.
Her remarks came as the West Bengal government has constituted a high-level committee to examine a draft Uniform Civil Code for the state. A government notification said the panel was formed in view of the "wide ramifications and voluminous nature" of the proposed legislation and would undertake a comprehensive examination of the draft Bill before any further steps are taken.
Referring to Bangladesh, the 63-year-old writer said equality was the cornerstone of civilisation, but many women continued to face discrimination. "In Bangladesh, Hindu women do not have equal rights. They cannot inherit their father's property. If Hindu women are to enjoy freedom and equal rights, a Uniform Civil Code is necessary," she said.
Nasreen was felicitated at a state government programme at Rabindra Sadan on Saturday after returning to Kolkata for the first time since 2007, when protests over the publication of her book Dwikhandito forced the then Left Front government to move her out of the city. She had left Bangladesh in 1994 after receiving death threats from radical groups over her writings and views on religion.
Recalling the disruption at Saturday's event, Nasreen said she felt "insulted" after Goswami was prevented from speaking. "Not only was Joy insulted, but I was also insulted because I had invited him," she said. The controversy erupted after she invited Goswami onto the stage and asked him to address the gathering, but loud objections from a section of the audience forced him to step down without speaking.
"In my speech, I had spoken about freedom of expression. Everyone should be allowed to speak. It is not right to stop anyone from expressing their views," she said. Questioning the conduct of those who objected, she added, "Those who appreciated my speech were the ones who did not allow him to come on the stage. Didn't they also question me? It is contradictory. When someone speaks about freedom of expression, people support it, but when a poet is invited to speak, they do not want to hear him. That is not right." She said she would visit Goswami at his residence, adding, "I have not got the opportunity to speak to Joy (after the incident), but I will pay him a visit today or tomorrow."
Nasreen said she hoped such an incident would not happen again in her favourite city. "Kolkata is a city of progressives. People here believe in freedom of speech and the right to express one's views. People's political ideologies may differ, but everyone must be given the space to express one's opinions," she said.
Asked to compare the Left Front, the Trinamool Congress and the present BJP government in West Bengal, Nasreen praised the BJP-led dispensation for allowing her to visit Kolkata.
"There is, of course, a difference between the three governments. One government expelled me, another did not allow me to return, while the third has allowed me to come. Instead of focusing on those differences, I think we should celebrate the fact that I have been able to come back. I am very happy that I could return. I want to believe that this government believes in the right to freedom of expression and freedom of speech," she said.
Nasreen said she had been invited to Kolkata by an organisation called Secular Mission and that the state government later provided her security cover and facilitated her visit to West Bengal. On Saturday, she had said her return after 19 years showed that "injustice can be long but cannot be permanent", while maintaining that her fight had always been for women's rights and freedom of expression, and not for or against any political party.
When asked whether she wanted to return to Kolkata permanently, Nasreen said she had not yet "give it thought" but wanted to come back for the Kolkata Book Fair next year. "I surely want to come to Kolkata Book Fair. The Bengal chief minister has promised me security. So, I will definitely try to come. I will," she said. Stressing again that her views were independent of politics, she added, "I travel to many states. If I visit Kerala, does that make me part of that state's politics? Certainly not. I remain independent. Any government that provides me security is only discharging its responsibility. That has nothing to do with politics."
Nasreen's visit to Kolkata combined a renewed call for a Uniform Civil Code with a strong defence of equal rights and free speech, even as she spoke about her difficult history with the city and her wish to return again for the Book Fair.

headline: Bhagwant Mann inaugurates 2 Schools of Eminence in Ludhiana, total reaches 16
full_text:
Bhagwant Mann inaugurates 2 Schools of Eminence in Ludhiana, total reaches 16
Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann dedicated two new Schools of Eminence in Ludhiana on Sunday. The move takes the district's total to 16 and underlines the state's push to expand quality public education.
Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann on Sunday dedicated two new Schools of Eminence at Kidwai Nagar and Miller Ganj in Ludhiana, taking the district's total number of such schools to 16.
The new campuses have modern classrooms, state-of-the-art laboratories, an auditorium and other advanced facilities. Mann said the schools are part of the Punjab government's efforts to strengthen public education and provide world-class learning infrastructure to students.
During his visit, the chief minister spent time interacting with students at the newly inaugurated schools. He visited classrooms, science laboratories and other academic facilities, took stock of the infrastructure, and spoke to students about their studies, scientific experiments and learning experience.
Addressing a gathering, Mann said sustained investment in education has transformed government schools into institutions of excellence. He said improved infrastructure, overseas teacher training and modern teaching practices have led to a growing preference for government schools among parents. He also said that after leading Punjab's industrial revolution, Ludhiana is now emerging as a frontrunner in the state's education revolution.
“The School of Eminence model has been instrumental in reducing the gap between the rich and the poor in access to quality education. Today, children from ordinary families are receiving facilities that are even better than those available in many private schools,” he said.
Mann said the school at Kidwai Nagar has been completed at a cost of Rs 10.62 crore, while the school at Miller Ganj has been completed at a cost of Rs 3.48 crore. He added, “No freebie or concession cards can eliminate poverty or other social maladies in the state, but education is the key that can pull people out of this vicious cycle by raising their standard of living.
Therefore, the government is tirelessly making efforts to improve the standard of education and empower the common people.” With the two new schools now dedicated, Ludhiana's Schools of Eminence network has expanded further as the state government pushes its public education programme.

headline: New Delhi: More than half of the overall respondents of the latest snap poll by CVoter were not satisfied with Modi government’s handling of the paper leaks issue, the polling agency said in a statement Sunday. This number was 40 percent among NDA vo...
full_text:
New Delhi: More than half of the overall respondents of the latest snap poll by CVoter were not satisfied with Modi government’s handling of the paper leaks issue, the polling agency said in a statement Sunday. This number was 40 percent among NDA voters.
The polling agency added that PM Narendra Modi Modi continues to command a 12-percentage point lead over Lok Sabha Leader of the Opposition Rahul Gandhi when it comes to ‘most popular youth leader among Indians’. It went further to add that opinion remains sharply divided over CJP’s demand for withdrawal of all FIRs against protesters.
The survey findings and projections are based on CVoter Snap Poll CATI (Computer Assisted Telephone Interviewing) interviews conducted among 18+ adults nationwide (BARC-HSM) between 29 and 30 July. The sample spread of 1,349 respondents is spread across all districts covering all states, said CVoter. According to the polling agency, the data is weighted to the known demographic profile as per the census and final ECI results.
“Though still far behind (Modi), Rahul Gandhi is gaining as the most popular youth leader,” read the statement by CVoter, adding that “anti-incumbency among the youth is a serious issue” and that while a “majority of Indians want proper investigations into alleged police brutality; a majority also (wants) police action against those who indulged in violence and were offensively abusive”.
The statement went on to add, “Overall, the paper leak and the CJP protests have inflicted political damage to the NDA government. But they are not the main challenge. The real challenge is the frustration of the youth whose rising aspirations are hitting a roadblock of limited opportunities.”
Protests spearheaded by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) over his handling of the NEET-UG (2026) paper leak last week forced the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan. The government also announced fast-track courts to deal with paper leak cases and steered an amendment to the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024, through both houses of Parliament, which proposes harsher punishment for those found using or facilitating unfair means.

58% NDA supporters want police brutality probed
According to the latest CVoter snap poll, 12 percent of respondents said they saw CJP being the voice of the youth and almost 50 percent said they would support the movement on other issues as well in the future.
As many as 31.7 percent of the respondents said stricter laws against paper leaks should have been the top priority for the government, followed by 27 percent who said it should have been Pradhan’s resignation, and 17 percent who said formation of an expert panel should have been top priority.
Were they satisfied with the discussion in Parliament on paper leaks? According to the polling agency, 35 percent of respondents were satisfied and 39 percent weren’t.
Opinion was sharply divided, however, on CJP’s demand for withdrawal of all FIRs against students who took part in demonstrations held across the country.
“On the face of it, a larger proportion of respondents (35.5 percent) want all FIRs to be withdrawn while less than one fourth say withdraw FIRs against only peaceful protestors. Significantly, more than one third of the respondents say investigative agencies should probe all FIRs first before arriving at a decision,” said CVoter.
However, 62.7 percent of respondents were of the opinion that allegations of police brutality during the protests must be investigated. “Interestingly, even almost 58 percent of those who support the NDA want a proper investigation,” the polling agency said.
At the same time, 54.2 percent of respondents want the police to act against protesters who used abusive language and uploaded objectionable content on social media. Among INDIA bloc supporters, 45 percent back police action in this regard.
For 27.6 percent of respondents, student anger over paper leaks was the trigger that earned the CJP its support. “Close to 50 percent of the respondents say they will support (CJP for other causes too) while less than 30 percent say they won’t. Almost 38 percent of NDA voters say they will support future CJP protests and movements,” CVoter said.

MNS chief Raj Thackeray on Sunday launched a sharp attack on industrialists and public figures who praise Prime Minister Narendra Modi and the BJP government while choosing to live abroad, questioning their claims that India had improved significantly under the current administration. Speaking at the 20th anniversary rally of the Maharashtra Navnirman Vidyarthi Sena in Mumbai, Thackeray cited actors Vivek Oberoi and R Madhavan as examples and linked their decisions to what he described as growing frustration among the country's youth.Claiming that the government had itself acknowledged in Parliament that entrepreneurs were leaving India, Thackeray argued that many of those who publicly endorse the government's narrative were unwilling to build their own lives in the country.

headline: A man threw a slipper at Independent MP Pappu Yadav during a press conference at his house on Sunday (August 2, 2026) after the lawmaker defended his skit inside the Parliament House complex on the alleged theft of donations at the Ram temple, leadin...

A man threw a slipper at Independent MP Pappu Yadav during a press conference at his house on Sunday (August 2, 2026) after the lawmaker defended his skit inside the Parliament House complex on the alleged theft of donations at the Ram temple, leading to a scuffle between his supporters and the attacker.
Mr. Yadav was addressing the presser amid a row over his Friday (July 31, 2026) protest with an FIR being filed in Varanasi against him, Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi and Samajwadi Party MP from Faizabad (Ayodhya) Awadhesh Prasad for allegedly hurting religious sentiments.
While Mr. Yadav was addressing the presser, a man questioned him over his actions and alleged that the MP had insulted Lord Ram. He then threw a slipper at Mr. Yadav, and a scuffle ensued between the Purnia MP’s supporters and the attacker.
Mr. Yadav later alleged that it was an attempt on his life.
According to police sources, the alleged attacker was identified as 34-year-old Sumit, a native of Uttar Pradesh’s Bulandshahr, who works in an iron fabrication business in Ghaziabad and has no previous criminal record.
The police source said that another man, identified as Happy, was present in an SUV parked outside Yadav’s residence when the incident occurred.
Investigators are verifying their claims and probing the motive behind the incident.
Rajesh Ranjan alias Pappu Yadav, dressed in a saffron outfit, performed the skit on Friday (July 31, 2026) in the Parliament House complex along with other Opposition MPs in front of the Makar Dwar at the Parliament complex to protest the alleged embezzlement of donations at the Ram temple in Ayodhya.
The MPs, including Rahul Gandhi, put money inside donation boxes, while Mr. Yadav slipped money into his pockets to symbolise the alleged theft at the Ram temple.
The BJP on Sunday (August 2, 2026) accused Mr. Gandhi and Mr. Yadav of hurting Hindu sentiments and demanded that they publicly apologise.
However, a defiant Yadav said they were protesting to protect Sanatan and will not be cowed down by any number of FIRs.
He was reacting a day after a case was filed in Varanasi on the complaint of seers against him, Mr. Gandhi and Samajwadi Party MP from Faizabad (Ayodhya) Awadhesh Prasad while BJP MP Bansuri Swaraj and other leaders filed a police complaint in Delhi.
The RSS affiliate Vishva Hindu Parishad (VHP) also attacked Mr. Gandhi and Mr. Yadav, alleging that the two leaders insulted Sanatan Dharma through the protest staged in the Parliament complex.

Judge leading fast-track paper leak court transferred by Delhi HC
NEW DELHI: The Delhi High Court has transferred Special Judge Anu Grover Baliga, who was appointed last month to head the designated fast-track court for paper leak cases, as part of a reshuffle involving 138 judicial officers.Judge Baliga was appointed after the Delhi High Court, on July 23, designated a special court to hear criminal cases related to paper leaks and other unfair practices in public examinations, as cited by PTI.
Baliga had spent just over a week at the designated paper leak court after assuming charge on July 25. Special Judge Ajay Gupta, who had earlier been hearing paper leak cases, including the NEET matter, will replace her.According to the Delhi High Court's transfer order issued on Saturday, Judge Baliga has been posted to a special court constituted under the National Investigation Agency (NIA) Act to hear terrorism-related cases.The High Court also appointed Special Judges Vikas Dhull, Prashant Sharma, Pulastya Pramachala, Kiran Bansal and Amit Bansal to NIA courts dealing with terror cases.Prime Minister Narendra Modi had announced the setting up of fast-track courts to ensure the swift disposal of cases related to paper leaks.
Following the announcement, a designated fast-track court was established at Delhi's Rouse Avenue Courts to hear cases under the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024, and other related offences. All such cases were ordered to be transferred to the designated court.
The court held its first hearing in the NEET paper leak case on July 27, but the proceedings were adjourned at the request of the defence counsel. The matter was then listed for Monday for consideration of the CBI's chargesheet and the bail pleas of two accused.On May 12, the National Testing Agency (NTA) cancelled the National Eligibility-cum-Entrance Test (Undergraduate), or NEET-UG, conducted on May 3 for medical admissions following allegations of a paper leak. full_text:
Delhi High Court transfers judge hearing paper leak cases to anti-terror court
While Judge Anu Grover Baliga has been transferred to a Special NIA Court, her place in the anti-paper leak court will be taken by Judge Ajay Gupta. The transfers are part of a massive reshuffle ordered by the Delhi High Court, which reassigned 138 judicial officers across various courts in the national capital.

While she has been transferred to a Special NIA Court, her place in the anti-paper leak court will be taken by Judge Ajay Gupta. The transfers are part of a massive reshuffle ordered by the Delhi High Court, which reassigned 138 judicial officers across various courts in the national capital.
The move has cleared the way for the posting of judges in several newly established special courts, including those for trial in cases pertaining to the National Investigation Agency (NIA), the Maharashtra Control of Organised Crime Act (MCOCA) and the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act.
Besides Judge Baliga, five other judges – Vikas Dhull, Prashant Sharma, Amit Bansal, Kiran Bansal and Pulastya Pramachala – will assume charge as Special NIA judges.
The mass transfer order came roughly a week after Judge Baliga's court was designated by the Delhi High Court as the dedicated court to hear criminal cases under the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024 on July 23 this year.
The notification came hours after Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced that fast-track courts would be established to ensure speedy trials and strict action against those involved in examination paper leak cases. The announcement was made amid a growing agitation over NEET-related irregularities.
NEW NIA COURTROOMS TO BE INAUGURATED
The newly constructed NIA courtrooms at the Rouse Avenue Courts Complex are scheduled to be inaugurated on Monday, August 3, marking the shift of all anti-terror trials out of the Patiala House Courts Complex.
In addition to the NIA courts, dedicated MCOCA and NDPS courts have also been established at Rouse Avenue. Four judges—Sandeep Yadav, Anuradha Shukla, Devendra Kumar Sharma and Bhupinder Singh—have been posted as Special Exclusive NDPS judges, while Gaurav Rao, Gagandeep Singh and Surbhi Sharma Vats have been appointed as Special Exclusive MCOCA judges.
All the new postings mentioned in the order, issued on Saturday, August 1, will be applicable with effect from Tuesday, August 4.

headline: GST collections cross ₹2.11 lakh crore in July
full_text:
GST collections cross ₹2.11 lakh crore in July
The GST regime entered its 10th year with a monthly gross GST collection of ₹2,11,205 crore as against ₹1,83,065 crore in July 2025.
India’s gross Goods and Services Tax collections in July crossed ₹2 lakh crore for the second time in the current fiscal year with 15.4% year-on-year jump to surpass ₹2.11 lakh crore, which is the third highest monthly collection since the GST regime was unveiled on July 1, 2017.
The GST regime entered its 10th year with a monthly gross GST collection of ₹2,11,205 crore as against ₹1,83,065 crore in July 2025, reflecting India’s economic resilience, steady domestic consumption and effective compliances, according to finance ministry data released on Saturday.
Also Read | Punjab’s first-quarter GST collection logs 24% jump
Domestic transactions collections
Collections from domestic transactions rose 10.1% in July to ₹1,44,695 crore from ₹1,31,439 crore a year earlier, while revenues from imports jumped 28.8% to ₹66,511 crore from ₹51,626 crore.
Net GST collection in July 2026, after refunds, also saw a robust double-digit growth, which stood at ₹1,81,237 crore in July 2026, registering 15.8% jump from ₹1,56,570 crore in July 2025. Total refunds rose 13.1% to ₹29,968 crore from ₹26,495 crore in July last year.
To be sure, the July collections relate to business transactions undertaken in June.
Also Read | Pre-GST tax disputes: Punjab extends OTS scheme till Sept 30
What experts say
Deloitte India partner MS Mani said: “The high GST collections which reflect business transactions during June 26 ties up very well with the 7.3% increase in industrial production during June. It reflects continued economic resilience despite the challenges in the external environment.”
Experts, however, pointed at high growth in monthly GST collections on imports, which could be either because of imports of inputs for domestic value-addition or for purely consumption.
Also Read | GST refund fraud: Three Delhi tax officials among five held in ₹5.5 crore scam
EY India tax partner Saurabh Agarwal said, “One cannot ignore the elevated levels of import GST collections, which remain a nagging concern. This points to a persistent gap in domestic manufacturing capability despite the range of successful PLI [production linked incentive] and Atmanirbhar Bharat interventions rolled out over the past few years.”

headline: Illegal sale of unauthorised army-pattern combat clothes busted in Rajasthan's Sriganganagar
full_text:
Illegal sale of unauthorised army-pattern combat clothes busted in Rajasthan's Sriganganagar
The Indian army had earlier secured a patent for a new combat uniform unveiled in 2022 to prevent unauthorised sale and misuse.
In a joint operation targeting the illegal sale of battle fatigues, the Indian Army and Rajasthan Police seized nearly 1,000 metres of unauthorised army-pattern combat cloth from multiple shops in Rajasthan’s Sriganganagar town, the army said on Saturday.
The seizure points to a wider network supplying counterfeit military uniforms to vendors in the region, it added.
To be sure, the army earlier secured a patent for a new combat uniform unveiled in 2022 to prevent unauthorised sale and misuse. The new digital camouflage pattern uniform was introduced to address the uncontrolled proliferation of an earlier uniform, which led to security vulnerabilities in military establishments.
The action followed the seizure of similar counterfeit combat cloth in Bareilly in June this year, which the army traced to a manufacturer in Sriganganagar. “Acting on this lead, Indian Army intelligence personnel conducted a discreet investigation in the city, which pointed to a local firm as a key link in the supply chain allegedly distributing counterfeit Army-pattern combat cloth to shops in Sriganganagar town as well as in Lalgarh Jattan, Suratgarh and other nearby markets,” it said.
An interim probe report was shared with Rajasthan Police in mid-July, leading to a coordinated operation on July 30 in which security personnel and police searched multiple shops across the district. Unauthorised possession, sale or use of military-pattern combat cloth is a punishable offence. Such material poses a security risk because it enables the impersonation of armed forces personnel, the army added.
Also read: Waste dumped at Okhla landfill till 2025 cleared: Delhi government
Another reason for selecting the new uniform pattern was to introduce uniformity in soldiers’ battle fatigues. Variations in the earlier uniform pattern drew criticism from several quarters. The National Institute of Fashion Technology helped the army finalise the new combat uniform. While soldiers wear the combat uniform in operational areas, those posted at the Army headquarters in New Delhi also wear the combat dress on Fridays in solidarity with personnel in forward areas.

headline: Army, Rajasthan Police bust fake uniform racket, 1,000m cloth seized
full_text:
Army, Rajasthan Police bust fake uniform racket, 1,000m cloth seized
Army intelligence units and Rajasthan Police uncovered an alleged fake military cloth supply network in Sriganganagar. Officials said the unauthorised fabric poses a security risk because it can aid impersonation.
A joint operation by Indian Army intelligence units and Rajasthan Police has uncovered an alleged counterfeit military uniform supply network in Rajasthan's Sriganganagar district, leading to the seizure of nearly 1,000 metres of unauthorised Army-pattern combat cloth from multiple shops.
The operation stemmed from a June seizure of counterfeit combat cloth in Bareilly, which investigators traced back to a manufacturing source in Sriganganagar. Following the lead, Indian Army intelligence personnel conducted a discreet investigation that identified a local firm as a key link in the supply chain allegedly distributing fake Army-pattern combat fabric across the region.
According to officials, the firm was suspected of supplying counterfeit military-pattern cloth to vendors in Sriganganagar town as well as markets in Lalgarh Jattan, Suratgarh and nearby areas.
LEAD FROM BAREILLY SEIZURE TRIGGERED PROBE
After gathering evidence, Army intelligence units shared an interim investigation report with Rajasthan Police in mid-July. Based on the findings, a coordinated operation was launched on July 30, with police and security personnel carrying out searches at multiple shops across the district.
The raids resulted in the recovery of around 1,000 metres of unauthorised new-pattern combat cloth resembling material used for military uniforms.
SECURITY RISK DUE TO POTENTIAL IMPERSONATION
Officials said the unauthorised possession, sale or use of military-pattern combat fabric is a punishable offence. Such counterfeit material poses a significant security threat as it can be used to impersonate armed forces personnel and facilitate unlawful activities.
Investigators are now probing the extent of the supply network and whether the counterfeit cloth was being distributed beyond Rajasthan to other parts of the country.

headline: Anybody who backs delimitation is betraying Tamil Nadu, says Rahul Gandhi
full_text:
Anybody who backs delimitation is betraying Tamil Nadu, says Rahul Gandhi
He urged all parties in the state to oppose the proposal, alleging it would weaken Tamil Nadu’s voice in national politics.
Congress leader and Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi on Saturday alleged that the BJP-led Centre’s proposed delimitation exercise was aimed at reducing Tamil Nadu’s political influence and urged all parties to oppose it in Parliament.
Speaking to reporters at Mamallapuram near Chennai after attending the concluding session of a 10-day training camp for District Congress Committee presidents, he described the move as a “conspiracy” against Tamil Nadu. “It is a very important issue for the future of the Tamil people, the Tamil language and the state of Tamil Nadu. BJP is attempting to carry out delimitation, which is designed to disenfranchise and take away power from the Tamil people. This is a BJP conspiracy,” Gandhi said.
He urged all parties in the state to oppose the proposal, alleging it would weaken Tamil Nadu’s voice in national politics.
“Anybody who supports delimitation is betraying Tamil Nadu and is allowing RSS and the BJP to attack the people of Tamil Nadu,” he said.

“No Tamil person should support delimitation. Every single Tamil party, national party should defeat delimitation (bill) in Parliament,” Gandhi added.
Drawing a parallel with Ettappan, the 18th-century Tamil ruler of Ettayapuram who is widely remembered in Tamil history for allegedly aiding the British against freedom fighter Veerapandiya Kattabomman, Gandhi said, “Anybody who supports delimitation is a 21st-century Ettappan.”
Earlier in the day, Gandhi met families of students who allegedly died by suicide over issues related to NEET and asserted that students are told to work honestly in a system that is not honest with them.
After the interaction, he said on X, “Nothing is more painful than seeing a parent grieve for their child. Behind every young life lost is a family carrying pain that will never leave them — and serious questions about a broken education system.”
Targeting PM Narendra Modi, he said, “He has not met a single grieving parent. He has not sat with a single student whose future was stolen by a leaked paper. India’s students do not need his forgiveness. They are owed his apology.”
Responding to Gandhi’s remarks on delimitation, state BJP spokesperson Narayanan Thirupathy accused him of making irresponsible statements.
“Here is a person who is so irresponsible, trying to create unrest in the country, supporting anarchists and wanting to divide the nation as the Congress did during Partition,” he said.

headline: RTI activist seeks inquiry into how Abhijeet Dipke's father funded his US education
full_text:
RTI activist seeks inquiry into how Abhijeet Dipke's father funded his US education
A Surat-based RTI activist has called for a probe into the CJP and the finances of founder Abhijeet Dipke's father, as well as the legal aid pledged.
Days after the Cockroach Janta Party announced a legal fund of ₹1 crore for protestors arrested or detained by Delhi Police, an RTI activist has sought an inquiry into the funds for the online outfit.
A Surat-based RTI activist has called for a probe into the CJP and the finances of founder Abhijeet Dipke's father.
As per a report by news agency PTI, activist Amit Tiwari sought an inquiry into the finances of Bhagwanrao Dipke, who is a retired Maharashtra government employee. The inquiry comes due to Dipke's education in the United States.
Abhijeet Dipke, a graduate from Boston University, returned to India on June 6 to kick off the protests led by the Cockroach Janta Party.
"I have also complained to the Maharashtra Government that Bhagwanrao Dipke was a Junior Engineer at MIDC. So, if he received a salary of ₹60,000-65,000, how was he able to afford the education of his children in the US?" he said.
"We have complained to the Maharashtra Government that this should be investigated and strict action should be taken if this is a case of disproportionate assets," Tiwari added.
CJP's legal aid also under scanner
The activist also wrote to the Election Commission of India and the Central GST over the legal defence fund announced by senior advocate and Rajya Sabha MP Kapil Sibal.
"The Cockroach Janta Party is an unregistered entity but is operating as a political party....If ₹1 crore has been pledged to it as a legal defence fund, then the EC should verify whether the CJP is registered with it under section 29A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951," he was quoted as saying by PTI.
He added that if the outfit is not registered, then its collection of funds needs to be examined.
The activist also inquired where Kapil Sibal will pay the 18 per cent GST on the ₹1 crore pledged as legal aid.
He also criticised the CJP-led protests, saying the movement had crossed a line after initially being centred on the NEET paper leak issue.
"We respect our elders. It was fine until you were carrying out the CJP movement and protesting over NEET. But in the middle of the agitation, you started abusing PM Modi and his late mother. You also spoke foul on his ties to foreign leaders. We have complained against all of this. It is all wrong," he was quoted as saying by news agency ANI.

headline: July GST collections up 15.4% to Rs 2.1 L cr on higher imports
full_text:
July GST collections up 15.4% to Rs 2.1 L cr on higher imports
TNN / Aug 02, 2026, 02:46 IST
Comments
Share
AA
Text Size
Small
Medium
Large
NEW DELHI: GST collections rose 15.4% to Rs 2,11,205 crore in July, the second highest since the new structure was implemented last Sept, on the back of a 29% jump in integrated GST (IGST) on imports. This was also the highest pace of growth since rate rationalisation.The rise in IGST on imports in July (for transactions in the previous month) may be attributed to higher prices of crude and other commodities in the wake of the West Asia conflict.The impact of strong economic activity in June, when factory output grew at its fastest pace in nearly two years, was also visible on the tax numbers, seen as an advance indicator of economic activity. Some of the price hikes in FMCG and automobile sectors would have also buoyed collections. Central GST mop-up was pegged 12.3% higher at just under Rs 40,000 crore, while state GST grew 8.7% to nearly Rs 48,000 crore."The high GST collections tie in very well with the 7.3% increase in industrial production during June. It reflects continued economic resilience despite the challenges in the external environment...The
steady growth in GST collections each month indicates that overall domestic consumption is becoming largely insulated from seasonal variations and external headwinds," said MS Mani, partner at Deloitte India.Some experts, however, are worried about the continued rise in imports. "...one cannot ignore the elevated levels of import GST collections, which remain a nagging concern. This points to a persistent gap in domestic manufacturing capability despite the range of successful PLI and Atmanirbhar Bharat interventions rolled out over the past few years.
It is likely that the sustained push by policymakers towards localisation of around 100 products (being talked about) over a period of time will help bridge this gap," said Saurabh Agarwal, partner at EY India, a consulting firm.Net of refunds, which were 13% higher at almost Rs 30,000 crore, collections went up 15.8% to Rs 1,81,237 crore.Haryana logged the highest growth of 28%, followed by Gujarat and Puducherry (26%), Karnataka and Goa (23%), and Maharashtra (20%). Chhattisgarh (23% fall), Jharkhand and Manipur (20% decline) were among the laggards.

headline: Punjab Congress chief dismisses pro-Channi slogan row, blames AAP and TV channels
full_text:
Punjab Congress chief dismisses pro-Channi slogan row, blames AAP and TV channels
Punjab Congress chief Raja Warring dismissed the pro-Channi slogans raised at recent party events. The episode has again exposed factional strains as the party prepares for the 2027 Assembly polls.
Punjab Congress chief Amrinder Singh Raja Warring on Sunday played down the pro-Charanjit Singh Channi slogans raised at party events over the past two days, and accused the Aam Aadmi Party and television channels of blowing up the issue. He said the ruling party was presenting the slogans as something far more serious, while channels were focusing only on the sloganeering.
Warring made the remarks while speaking to reporters in Barnala after supporters of Jalandhar MP and former chief minister Charanjit Singh Channi interrupted the Congress's "Har Booth, Congress Mazboot" programme with slogans in Channi's favour.
AICC general secretary in-charge of Punjab Bhupesh Baghel was present at the event. Similar slogans were also raised at programmes attended by Baghel in Patiala and Sangrur on Saturday.
Referring to the controversy, Warring said, "The current (AAP) government is presenting the slogans raised in favour of Charanjit Singh Channi as if they were chanted in favour of Pakistan." He also blamed television channels for showing only the sloganeering and ignoring the rest of the events. "No television channel is showing that a leader from Shutrana joined the Congress on Saturday, or that 40-50 AAP MLAs are likely to switch sides," he alleged.
Warring said his own speech at the event had been heard by party workers and had received applause, but had not been shown on television. "I gave a speech, and everybody listened to it. The party workers clapped. But no TV channel is showing it," he said, asking what objection the media and the AAP had if a slogan was raised.
"What happens if a slogan is raised? Channi had been our chief minister. I myself had raised the slogan 'Ghar Ghar Challi Gal, Channi Karda Masle Hal' (Go from house to house and say, Channi does resolve problems). I had raised slogans in favour of Partap Singh Bajwa also," he said.
As he sought to end the row, Warring shouted before the media, "Charanjit Singh Channi Zindabad." The developments come at a time when the Punjab Congress is dealing with factionalism despite repeated statements from the party leadership that it is working to strengthen organisational unity ahead of the 2027 Punjab Assembly polls.
The tensions had become visible after the Congress leadership on July 1 retained Warring as state unit chief and appointed Channi as chairperson of its campaign committee.

headline: DMK moves SC, seeks immediate Cauvery water release by Karnataka
full_text:
DMK moves SC, seeks immediate Cauvery water release by Karnataka
Pointing out the urgency of the situation, the DMK said, “The present period is the most crucial period of the entire water year for the Cauvery Delta
The Opposition Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) on Saturday moved the Supreme Court (SC) seeking a direction to Karnataka to immediately release Cauvery water to Tamil Nadu and comply with the binding directions issued by the Cauvery Water Management Authority (CWMA).
The move comes even as the Tamil Nadu government is in the process of filing an appeal before the Supreme Court.
The application, filed by DMK Farmers Wing secretary and former MP A.K.S. Vijayan, comes amid concerns over a water crisis in the state during a crucial phase of the agricultural season in the Cauvery Delta.
Also Read | Embattled NTA floats ₹7.5 crore tender for round-the-clock security at HQ, regional offices
Pointing out the urgency of the situation, the DMK said, “The present period is the most crucial period of the entire water year for the Cauvery Delta, and it is precisely now that the water is required to flow.”
It said the current period is critical for raising the Kuruvai (short-term) paddy crop and for undertaking preparatory and transplantation operations for the Samba (long-term) crop in the Cauvery Delta. “If water is not realised at Biligundlu now, the standing Kuruvai crop will wither before harvest, the ensuing Samba cultivation — the mainstay of the Delta — will equally be imperilled for want of both river flows and groundwater, and the fertile Cauvery Delta, the rice bowl of Tamil Nadu, faces the real and imminent danger of being reduced to a desert,” the application stated.
Also Read | ‘Being a Gurkha’: Mountaineer Nirmal Purja ‘Dai’, killed by Pak avalanche, had ‘only one dream’
The DMK moved the apex court seeking urgent directions to the Karnataka government to comply with the Cauvery Water Regulation Committee’s (CWRC) July 28 direction to release 3,500 cusecs of water per day at Biligundlu for 15 days commencing July 29. Karnataka had challenged the order before the CWMA, but its appeal was dismissed on July 30.
The application, settled by senior advocate P Wilson, pointed out that Tamil Nadu had informed the CWRC that Karnataka was not releasing water in line with the Supreme Court’s earlier decision as well as a tribunal directing it to maintain a monthly stipulated flow during the months of June to January totalling to 167.25 TMC (thousand million cubic feet). According to the plea, Tamil Nadu had told the CWRC that Karnataka must first release a backlog of about 9.46 TMC.
However, Karnataka opposed the demand and sought that the matter be kept in abeyance, citing acute distress, shortfall in inflows, low reservoir storage, drinking water requirements and conveyance losses.
The DMK claimed that even the CWRC order, later upheld by the CWMA, requiring Karnataka to ensure a flow of 3,500 cusecs per day at Biligundlu for 15 days would aggregate to about 4.5 TMC, which is far below Tamil Nadu’s entitlement even on a distress-sharing basis.
It said about 14.913 lakh acres in the Cauvery Delta depend on irrigation from the Mettur reservoir, which in turn depends on flows realised at Biligundlu from water released by Karnataka.

NEW DELHI: Stepping up his campaign against the rollout of E20 fuel, AAP national convener Arvind Kejriwal Saturday announced a march to PMâs residence Tuesday to submit petitions against the ethanol-blended fuel programme, while demanding that consumers be given the option to choose betw-een pure petrol and E20 at fuel stations.Addressing AAPâs âNational Townhall Against E20â at Constitution Club, Kejriwal alleged Centre had âimposedâ ethanol-blended fuel on consumers without adequate consultation and claimed it was causing financial losses to vehicle owners. He said petitions would be collected Monday, before a delegation of about 100 people marches to PMâs residence the following day.Kejriwal placed three demands before Centre -- provide both pure petrol and E20 at fuel stations, price E20 lower than pure petrol, and reduce petrol prices to below Rs 84 per litre. He argued that consumers should be free to decide which fuel they wish to purchase.Claiming govt has repeatedly maintained E20 is safe for vehicles, Kejriwal challenged Centre to make public the scientific studies supporting the policy. âGovt keeps saying studies have found E20 does not damage vehicles. If such studies exist, they should place the reports in the public domain,â he said, adding that several people had shared experiences of reduced mileage and vehicle problems during the town hall.
He also alleged govt was only delaying the introduction of higher ethanol blends like E25 and E30 until the controversy surrounding E20 subsides. âThere are no studies going on. They are simply waiting for the issue to die down. Once it settles, they will bring E25, E30 and continue increasing the ethanol content,â Kejriwal claimed, advising consumers to opt for electric vehicles until E100-compatible vehicles become commercially available.At the town hall, several owners, mechanics, delivery workers and experts claimed E20 had affected vehicle performance, increased maintenance costs and reduced mileage. His wife, who works in the automobile sector, claimed dealerships were receiving complaints from owners of newly-purchased vehicles regarding mileage and performance, but employees had no clear answers to offer.
Motorcycle mechanic Aamir Khan, who has been repairing petrol vehicles for over a decade at Bhalswa Dairy, claimed he had witnessed a rise in complaints, particularly from owners of older BS-III and BS-IV vehicles. He advised owners to keep their fuel tanks relatively full to minimise air and moisture accumulation inside the tank.Dr Anupam Saini, an environmental scientist from DU, questioned the environmental benefits of ethanol, saying any assessment should account for fertiliser use, water consumption, land-use change and the overall carbon footprint of ethanol production rather than tailpipe emissions alone.

headline: Congress MP asks 'Who was Modi's Sita?' during Ram Temple rituals, BJP hits back
full_text:
Congress MP asks 'Who was Modi's Sita?' during Ram Temple rituals, BJP hits back
Congress MP Pramod Tiwari questioned the absence of Goddess Sita during Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Ram Temple consecration rituals. He also sought a Supreme Court-monitored SIT probe into alleged donation embezzlement at the shrine.
Congress MP Pramod Tiwari on Sunday took a swipe at Prime Minister Narendra Modi over the Ram Temple consecration ceremony, questioning the absence of Goddess Sita during the rituals and asking, "Who was Ram's Sita then, and who is PM Modi's Sita?"
Addressing a press conference in New Delhi, Tiwari alleged that the Prime Minister prioritised electoral gains over religious traditions by inaugurating the temple before its completion.
"Modi was fonder of the election than the temple. He conducted rituals at an incomplete temple, which was inauspicious. The mandap was not built, the flag was not hoisted," Tiwari said.
Drawing a comparison with the Ramayana, the senior Congress leader said, "Even when Lord Ram performed the Ashwamedha Yagna, he had a stone idol of Goddess Sita placed beside him before the rituals began. When Modi performed the temple consecration, we couldn't see Goddess Sita anywhere. Who was Ram's Sita at that time, and who is PM Modi's Sita? The Prime Minister should answer that himself."
TIWARI ASKS FOR SUPREME COURT-MONITORED SIT
Tiwari also demanded a Supreme Court-monitored Special Investigation Team (SIT) probe into the alleged embezzlement of donations at the Ram Mandir, accusing the BJP of attempting to bury the controversy.
"This matter is linked to the faith and sentiments of crores of people. The investigation should be conducted by an SIT under the supervision of the Supreme Court. Those who took small amounts have been caught, but those who took away boxfuls and vaultfuls are still beyond the reach of the law," he alleged.
Questioning the resignations of those associated with the temple trust, Tiwari asked, "If there was no responsibility, why did they resign?"
The remarks came after the Uttar Pradesh government constituted a fresh SIT, headed by Inspector General of Police Kiran S, to investigate the alleged embezzlement of offerings at the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Temple following directions from the Supreme Court.
BJP HITS BACK
BJP on Sunday hit back at the Congress over senior leader Pramod Tiwari's remarks on the Ram Temple consecration ceremony, accusing the party of repeatedly insulting Lord Ram and hurting the faith of devotees.
Responding to Tiwari's comments questioning the absence of Goddess Sita during the Ram Temple consecration, BJP spokesperson Manish Shukla alleged that the Congress had consistently sought to malign Lord Ram.
"From Pramod Tiwari to Rahul Gandhi, the entire Congress has always worked to insult and malign Lord Shri Ram," Shukla said.

Bandhs and protests in Karnataka

headline: On Monday, August 3, we will get a sense of the public mood in the country, or, to be specific, in Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) strongholds such as Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, and Bihar. Three Assembly seats, one in each of these States, held bypolls on...
full_text:
On Monday, August 3, we will get a sense of the public mood in the country, or, to be specific, in Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) strongholds such as Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, and Bihar. Three Assembly seats, one in each of these States, held bypolls on July 30.
The one that all of us should watch closely is Bankipur in Bihar’s capital city, Patna. Bankipur is the heart of the heartland. The outcome in this seat will provide an indication of heartland politics in the aftermath of the student protests that recently rocked the country. The seat was vacated by Nitin Nabin, the BJP’s national president, and Jan Suraj leader Prashant Kishor is contesting from the constituency, testing his caste-free, anti-BJP politics in one of the party’s strongest forts.
No BJP candidate has ever lost from this seat. Mr. Nabin himself won it four consecutive times, most recently in 2025. It is an urban constituency with a demographic composition that has long made the BJP appear invincible. Yet the party has been compelled to deploy all its might in this by-election. Hundreds of party leaders from within and outside Bihar have camped there, mobilising every resource at their disposal.
Why is this seat so important for the BJP, and why will Monday’s (August 3) result be indicative of the party’s standing?
Bankipur is the first election after the BJP took over the Chief Minister’s post from Nitish Kumar. The party won the 2025 Assembly election with Mr. Kumar as its leader, and he continued to command a strong following among Other Backward Classes (OBC) voters within the BJP-led National Democratic Alliance (NDA) in the State. Bankipur will test how the BJP fares when it is fully in command, with Mr. Kumar removed from the political scene.
Bankipur has 3.79 lakh voters, of whom about 1.6 lakh are upper-caste Hindus, the core of BJP support in the Hindi heartland. There are around 40,000 Yadavs and roughly the same number of Muslims. Yadav and Muslim voters usually tend to support the Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD), which has never been in contention for much more than a lakh votes here. There are around 50,000 Dalits. The anti-Yadav social polarisation that has been a defining feature of Bihar elections for several years has overwhelmingly worked in the BJP’s favour in this constituency.
Apart from that, Bankipur has also become a hotspot of Hindutva mobilisation. Mr. Nabin began organising large Ram Navami processions in the constituency, which observers estimate drew nearly a lakh participants last March. Muharram processions, in which Muslims gather in large numbers, have also long been a feature of the constituency. Though the two do not occur at the same time, there has been a sense of competitiveness between them, helping to keep communal divisions politically salient over the years.
Mr. Kishor’s candidacy and campaign have challenged this pattern. A Brahmin himself, Mr. Kishor has advanced a caste-free politics in the State, seeking votes on a development agenda. But identity politics still matters in Bihar. What became a concern for the BJP was that some caste arithmetic also appeared to shift in his favour. Since the RJD never stood a realistic chance in the constituency, and Mr. Kishor emerged as a viable alternative, a section of upper-caste voters appeared inclined towards him. Muslims found in him an attractive option, while non-Yadav OBCs seemed less enthusiastic about the NDA without Nitish Kumar. Given these factors, even a section of Yadav voters may have viewed Mr. Kishor as a credible choice.
All told, turnout was low, at 34.24%, representing a drop of more than seven percentage points from last year, and there were indications of remarkable social realignment.
Mr. Kishor told The Hindu on Saturday (August 1) that the State government had unleashed the police on polling day to suppress his voters. “The BJP knows that its communal politics is no longer working. So this time it tried to misuse the administration and the police. Still, they will get a shock on Monday.”
Regardless of who wins on Monday (August 3), there will be enough indicators to gauge the mood of the heartland. Patna University is located in Bankipur. Jayaprakash Narayan lived in the Kadam Kuan locality within the constituency. Gandhi Maidan, which has witnessed many turning points not only in Bihar’s politics but also in the political history of the country, is also in Bankipur.

All major problems in Uttar Pradesh would end only after the BJP was voted out of power, he said.

Negative BJP members have always been opposed to creativity as it (creativity) forges a new path against conventions and orthodoxies, which the BJP’s conservative thinking does not like at all since they fear the expression of creativity will further strengthen the ‘anti-establishment wave’. The BJP government in Uttar Pradesh had closed more than 26,000 government primary schools since assuming power in 2017, Mr. Yadav also alleged on Sunday, claiming this had been done to deny education to children from the PDA (Pichhda or Backward Class, Dalit, and Alpsankhyak or Minority) communities. “Uttar Pradesh had 1,13,938 government primary schools until March 2017, when the BJP came to power. headline: Mother of teen girl who abused PM Modi upset as 'FIR not withdrawn' despite apology, claims CJP
full_text:
Mother of teen girl who abused PM Modi upset as 'FIR not withdrawn' despite apology, claims CJP
Lawyer Ratna Singh said that the mother was relieved to hear that the CJP was backing her and said she would reach out whenever any assistance is required.
The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) has alleged that the FIR against a teen girl for allegedly abusing Prime Minister Narendra Modi during the anti-NEET paper leak protest at Delhi's Jantar Mantar has not been withdrawn, despite the girl apologising and PM Modi saying he has forgiven the kids.
Lawyer Ratna Singh, who is overseeing the legal wing of the CJP, said on Sunday that she spoke to the girl’s mother, adding that the mother has been distressed that, despite the teen releasing the apology video, the media has continued to “hound” the family with questions.
“On behalf of the Cockroach Janta Party, I assured her that no legal action will be taken against her child. I also assured her that we will extend every possible legal assistance and ensure the girl receives any counselling and support she may need during this difficult time,” Singh wrote on X.
A complaint had been filed against the girl at a Noida police station for allegedly using derogatory slogans during the July 23 protest. Noida Police registered a Zero FIR, which was later transferred to Parliament Street Police Station in New Delhi.
The girl's apology and PM's forgiveness
The girl had apologised for her remarks against PM Narendra Modi in a video, saying the incident was her “first and last mistake”.
“I came under the influence of some people at the protest and said a lot of bad things against the Prime Minister. I apologise to the entire country. I am so ashamed. I can't even look at myself. Please forgive me,” she said.
PM Modi on Friday said he was deeply hurt that even his late mother was targeted with abusive remarks during the protest at Jantar Mantar. He also expressed disappointment that "our daughters" had used such language, while urging people to forgive the "misguided children".
In a video message posted on Instagram late at night, he said he understood the anger that many people were feeling. However, he said this was the time to support young people and help them find the right path.
He said a few "naughty children" had used abusive language against him, adding that the words spoken had no place in a civilised society.
"Not only was I subjected to abusive language at Jantar Mantar, but even my late mother was abused there with filthy language. But abuses never solve anything; let's guide the misguided," he said.
"I want to forgive them. People make mistakes, but it was a cultural shock that our daughters are using such abusive language. We must forgive our youth who were misguided; after all, they are our children. It's our duty to show them the right path," he said.
Mother says grateful to PM Modi
The mother of the 15-year-old girl had earlier said she is grateful to PM Modi "for choosing to forgive" her daughter, adding that it has given the teen "a new life."
"PM Modi has shown his greatness by forgiving the child who used such filthy and obscene words. Today is her birthday, and PM Modi has given her the greatest gift: jeevandaan (the gift of life). Today, this girl has been reborn," she told news agency PTI.

headline: FIR not withdrawn despite apology: Mother of girl who abused PM seeks protection
full_text:
FIR not withdrawn despite apology: Mother of girl who abused PM seeks protection
Days after the 15-year-old apologised for using derogatory language against PM Modi, her mother said that the FIR against her has not been withdrawn despite her being a minor. If Prime Minister Modi has forgiven her, then the police should also close the matter and withdraw the FIR, the girl's mother said.
The mother of the 15-year-old girl whose video abusing Prime Minister Narendra Modi during a protest at Delhi's Jantar Mantar went viral has appealed for the FIR against her daughter to be withdrawn, saying the teenager has realised her mistake and is deeply ashamed.
She said that the FIR against the teenager, who had used extremely derogatory language against the Prime Minister, has not been withdrawn even though PM Modi had said that the "misguided children" should be forgiven and guided on the right path.
Speaking to India Today, the woman said her daughter should not have used abusive language against elders and apologised on her behalf to the entire country.
"My daughter made a mistake. She should not have abused people older than her. On behalf of my daughter, I apologise to the entire country. The most important thing for me is that today she realises her mistake and there is shame in her eyes," she said.
The mother said young people have every right to protest and raise their voices through demonstrations, social media or YouTube, but should avoid using abusive language. "Protests are a separate issue. Children should raise their voice, but they should not abuse elders. That is wrong," she said.
According to her, the girl had left home on July 23 saying she was going shopping ahead of her birthday on August 1. The family only learnt about the incident after relatives sent them the viral video.
The woman claimed the family has been forced to move from place to place after the video surfaced, alleging they have received no security or assistance from the authorities.
"We cannot step outside without covering our faces. Vehicles keep circling our neighbourhood. We have already left our previous residence and are constantly changing locations. We have received no protection and are struggling even for food," she alleged.
She further claimed that despite it becoming known that the girl is a minor, the FIR against her has not been withdrawn.
"No government help or protection has been provided. Even the FIR against my daughter has not been withdrawn. If it has been established that she is a minor, why is the FIR still there?" she asked.
Referring to the girl's public apology, the mother said, "If Prime Minister Modi has forgiven her, then the police should also close the matter and withdraw the FIR."
She also denied having links with any political party, saying the family's only demand is protection. "We are ordinary people. We don't understand politics or big political issues. We just want protection. The police has not contacted me regarding our safety," she said.
The mother said teenagers are easily influenced by their surroundings and social media, adding that her daughter got carried away by the atmosphere at the protest.
"Children between 12 and 18 are at a sensitive age. They have Instagram, Facebook and many other platforms. Sometimes, in the heat of the moment, they don't realise what they are saying because everyone around them is doing the same. Later, they understand what they have done," she said.
She reiterated that what mattered most to her was that her daughter now regrets her actions and understands that she spoke disrespectfully about someone much older than her.
The controversy began after a video of the girl making abusive remarks against Prime Minister Narendra Modi during a protest at Jantar Mantar went viral on social media. A Zero FIR was subsequently registered on July 29 at the Expressway police station in Uttar Pradesh's Gautam Buddh Nagar on the complaint of a Ghaziabad resident.
The girl later released a video apologising with folded hands, claiming she was 15 years old and had been influenced by others at the protest. She said she deeply regretted her remarks and appealed for forgiveness, calling it the "first and last mistake" of her life.
Based on the complaint, the case was registered under Sections 352 (intentional insult to provoke breach of peace), 353(1) (statements conducing to public mischief) and 356(1) (defamation) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita. A Zero FIR allows a complaint to be registered at any police station regardless of jurisdiction before being transferred to the appropriate police station for investigation.
Meanwhile, Delhi Police said that they have not registered an FIRn in connection with the incident and that no fresh case will be filed by it.

headline: Amid Cauvery row, DK Shivakumar thanks Vijay for delaying Bengaluru visit
full_text:
Amid Cauvery row, DK Shivakumar thanks Vijay for delaying Bengaluru visit
Joseph Vijay agreed to postpone his Bengaluru visit after D K Shivakumar asked for a deferment. The move came as Karnataka sought to ease tensions over the Cauvery dispute and preserve cordial ties.
Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay has agreed to postpone his proposed visit to Bengaluru following a request from Karnataka Chief Minister DK Shivakumar amid heightened tensions over the Cauvery water-sharing dispute. Shivakumar said the decision would help preserve cordial relations between the two neighbouring states at a sensitive time.
Speaking after an all-party meeting on the Cauvery issue in Bengaluru on Sunday, Shivakumar said he personally requested Vijay to defer his visit as public sentiment in Karnataka remained strong over the ongoing water dispute.
"I have great respect for him. Though he may be new to politics, he is a courageous leader," Shivakumar said.
He added that he congratulated Vijay on his political journey and requested that the visit be rescheduled so the two leaders could meet in a "better and more cordial atmosphere."
"I don't want anyone shouting against my friends. We should respect each other. We have to live together and work together. Ultimately, India is one," the Karnataka Chief Minister said.
Shivakumar also dismissed allegations that his government was favouring Tamil Nadu or the ruling TVK, asserting that Karnataka's interests remained his priority while maintaining friendly ties with the neighbouring state.
"For me, Tamil Nadu is one and Karnataka is one. Ultimately, we are one," he said.
MEKEDATU PROJECT, CAUVERY RELEASES
During the press conference, Shivakumar reiterated Karnataka's support for the proposed Mekedatu balancing reservoir project, describing it as a long-term solution to the Cauvery water dispute.
He claimed that nearly 90 per cent of the project's benefits would accrue to Tamil Nadu and maintained that water stored in the proposed reservoir could not be diverted to Bengaluru.
"If the Mekedatu reservoir is built, nearly 90 per cent of the benefit will go to Tamil Nadu, more than Karnataka," he said, inviting people to visit the project site to understand its benefits.
The Chief Minister also said Karnataka would continue to abide by the Supreme Court's directions and legal provisions while safeguarding the state's interests.
Referring to the Cauvery Water Management Authority's directive to release 3,500 cusecs of water to Tamil Nadu for 15 days, Shivakumar said the state was complying despite deficient rainfall and challenging conditions.
On the DMK's move to approach the Supreme Court over the issue, he said political parties were entitled to hold differing views. "We are closely watching the situation. We respect the sentiments of the people and the law of the country. As per the orders passed, we are releasing water, and I hope there will be no problem," he said.

headline: ‘Will the emperor show his degree?’: CJP's Abhijeet Dipke throws a dare after BJP worker questions his US education

The video comes amid an ongoing political row over Dipke's educational qualifications and the funding for his study in the US, after a BJP worker filed an RTI application seeking details. The BJP has not responded to Dipke's latest remarks immediately.

headline: 22 children die of Chandipura virus in Gujarat, 7 under treatment
full_text:
22 children die of Chandipura virus in Gujarat, 7 under treatment
Gujarat Health Minister Praful Panseriya said all confirmed patients are below the age of 15 and clarified that the infections are not concentrated in any one village or district.
The Chandipura virus has claimed the lives of 22 children in Gujarat this monsoon season, with 35 infections confirmed out of 184 suspected cases reported so far, state Health Minister Praful Panseriya said on Monday.
Test results of 11 samples are still awaited.
Seven children who tested positive are currently undergoing treatment at civil hospitals across the state, while six patients have recovered and been discharged. Children admitted to hospitals in Gandhinagar, Sabarkantha-Himmatnagar, Patan, Rajkot and Bhavnagar are receiving specialised treatment under the supervision of expert doctors, he said.
The minister said all confirmed patients are below the age of 15 and clarified that the infections are not concentrated in any one village or district. Cases have been reported from different parts of Gujarat, prompting health authorities to remain on high alert.
To curb the spread of the virus, health department teams have intensified surveillance and launched large-scale insecticide spraying, particularly in livestock-rearing areas where sandflies — the primary carriers of the virus — are commonly found. Residents have also been advised to seal cracks in mud houses and walls, which can serve as breeding spots for the insects.
The government has directed all government and private paediatric hospitals to immediately admit children showing symptoms such as high fever, vomiting, seizures or altered consciousness to intensive care units equipped with oxygen and ventilator support. Early treatment is crucial to prevent severe complications, including multiple organ failure, officials said.
There is currently no specific vaccine or antiviral treatment for the Chandipura virus.
Gujarat Health Minister Praful Panseriya urged people not to panic or pay attention to rumours and appealed to parents to seek immediate medical attention if children develop symptoms. He also asked citizens to cooperate with health teams conducting surveillance and preventive measures.
Chandipura encephalitis is a rare viral disease that primarily spreads through sandflies and causes inflammation of the brain. The virus was first identified in Chandipura village in Maharashtra's Nagpur district in 1965. It mainly affects children and can progress rapidly if not treated in time.

22 children dead in Gujarat's Chandipura virus outbreak; 35 infections confirmed

As many as 22 children have died due to Chandipura virus (CHPV) in Gujarat this monsoon season, with 35 cases testing positive out of 184 suspected infections, state health minister Praful Panseriya said on Monday.
Seven patients remain under treatment across civil hospitals in Gandhinagar, Rajkot, and other districts, and government and private paediatric facilities have been instructed to immediately admit symptomatic patients to ICU beds to prevent organ failure, he said.
"A total of 184 suspected cases have been registered in the state so far, out of which 35 cases have tested positive and the results of 11 samples are still pending," Panseriya said.
Out of the cases reported so far, 22 children have died due to Chandipura virus, he said. All patients are under 15 years of age, he added.
Children under treatment, cases spread across districts
Children who are admitted to civil hospitals in Gandhinagar, Sabarkantha-Himmatnagar, Patan, Rajkot and Bhavnagar are being provided the best and super-specialist treatment and doctors are monitoring their condition, Panseriya said.
He further noted that cases are being reported from different areas and not concentrated in a particular village.
State steps up surveillance, treatment
Health teams are spraying pesticides in areas where animal husbandry is practised to target sandflies, which are responsible for spreading the encephalitis virus, he said.
Government and private paediatric facilities have been instructed to admit patients with symptoms of the virus to ICU beds with oxygen and ventilator facilities and not delay treatment so that serious conditions like multiple organ failure can be prevented, he said.
What is Chandipura virus?
Chandipura encephalitis is a viral disease that spreads mainly by sandflies and other insects and causes inflammation of the brain. The virus was first isolated from a patient from Chandipura village in Nagpur district of Maharashtra in 1965.

headline: BJP chief Nitin Nabin reacts as Prashant Kishor wrests his family seat: ‘Unexpected’

BJP chief Nitin Nabin reacts as Prashant Kishor wrests his family seat: ‘Unexpected’
BJP national president Nitin Nabin thanked voters in Gujarat for helping the party retain the Manjalpur Assembly seat and congratulated workers on the victory.
BJP national president Nitin Nabin on Monday accepted the verdict in the three Assembly bypolls and said the party would conduct a detailed review after losing the Bankipur seat in Bihar and Datia in Madhya Pradesh.
On X, Nabin thanked voters in Gujarat for helping the BJP retain the Manjalpur Assembly seat and congratulated party workers on the victory.
"We accept the mandate received in today's three assembly by-elections," he said. Thanking the people of Manjalpur, Nabin congratulated its workers and office-bearers for the win.

Referring to the defeats in Bankipur and Datia, Nabin admitted that the BJP had fallen short of expectations.
"In Bankipur and Datia, we did not receive the expected mandate. We will conduct a thorough introspection of the election results in both these areas with complete seriousness," he said.
He added that the BJP would return to the people "with renewed energy and determination" and continue working to further strengthen their trust.
ALSO READ | From Jan Suraaj's zero to Bankipur victory: What changed for Prashant Kishor in Bihar within months
Why Bankipur mattered for Nitin Nabin
The Bankipur bypoll carried high political stakes for the BJP because it was held in the party's traditional stronghold and a seat closely associated with Nitin Nabin.
The constituency has remained with the BJP since 1995. Nitin Nabin himself represented Bankipur for four consecutive terms and built it into one of the party's safest urban seats in Bihar.
The bypoll became necessary after he resigned as an MLA following his elevation as the BJP's national president.
The BJP fielded Neeraj Kumar to retain the seat, but Jan Suraaj Party founder Prashant Kishor defeated him by 19,324 votes, handing the BJP one of its most significant electoral setbacks in Bihar in recent years.
Bankipur had long been considered a BJP bastion. In the 2025 Assembly election, the BJP won the seat by a margin of more than 50,000 votes.

‘We humbly accept’
After the results, Nabin told reporters that the Congress merely retained a seat it already held in Datia and pointed out that the BJP had increased its vote tally there by around 1,700 compared to the previous Assembly election.
“The public's trust in us in a democracy is evident - after the last Assembly election, winning all 29 out of 29 Lok Sabha seats was accomplished by the Bharatiya Janata Party for the first time since independence,” he said.
He also spoke of the party's recent electoral record, saying that the BJP won all 29 Lok Sabha seats in Madhya Pradesh, retained its Budhni Assembly seat in a bypoll and even wrested the Amarwara seat from the Congress.
"We presented our view, Congress presented their view, and whatever verdict the public gave, we humbly accept it," Nabin said and added that the BJP would return to the people with greater strength in the upcoming elections.

headline: Congress retains Madhya Pradesh's Datia seat; BJP loses bypoll after candidate switch
full_text:
Congress retains Madhya Pradesh's Datia seat; BJP loses bypoll after candidate switch
At the end of all 15 rounds of counting, Singh secured 66,757 votes, while Tiwari polled 60,741 votes.
The Congress on Monday retained the Datia assembly seat in Madhya Pradesh, with the party candidate Ghanshyam Singh defeating his nearest rival Ashutosh Tiwari of the BJP by 6,016 votes in the byelection marked by differences in the saffron camp over the choice of candidate.
At the end of all 15 rounds of counting, Singh secured 66,757 votes, while Tiwari polled 60,741 votes. Azad Samaj Party candidate Damodar Yadav secured third position by bagging 22,527 votes, District Election Officer and Datia District Magistrate Swapnil Wankhade told PTI.
A total of 21 candidates were in the fray, including Ghanshyam Singh and Ashutosh Tiwari.
At one point, Singh's lead of 12,607 votes over his nearest rival appeared unassailable, but the BJP nominee managed to close the gap to an extent in the last rounds.
The byelection was necessitated after a Delhi court in April this year sentenced sitting Congress MLA Rajendra Bharti to three years' imprisonment in a cheating case, leading to the termination of his Assembly membership.
"This verdict marks the beginning of the end of the BJP," Ghanshyam Singh told reporters.
In Bhopal, celebrations broke out at the state Congress headquarters with party workers distributing sweets.
A total of 21 candidates contested the by-election, which saw a healthy 71.44 per cent voter turnout, though the main fight was between Congress' Singh and Tiwari of the ruling BJP.
Then-Congress nominee Bharti had defeated BJP candidate and former state Home Minister Narottam Mishra in Datia by over 7,700 votes in the 2023 Assembly elections.
For the by-election, the BJP denied a ticket to Mishra and instead fielded Tiwari.
Ghanshyam Singh expressed confidence that the Congress will form the next government in Madhya Pradesh in 2028, adding that the party was working to see Rahul Gandhi become the next Prime Minister.
He said his priority would be to promote communal harmony in Datia and end political vendetta.
"I will work to end gambling and betting rackets in the constituency," he said.
State Congress President Jitu Patwari described it as a victory for the people of Datia, a clarion call for the 2028 assembly elections, and the result of the collective efforts of Congress leaders.
Patwari told reporters in Bhopal that Datia voters have exposed the corruption, terror, and arrogance of the BJP-led government.
He said the people of Datia have laid the foundation for change and the BJP's departure.
