headline: Prashant Kishor rules out alliances after Bankipur win, says BJP voters backed him
full_text:
Prashant Kishor rules out alliances after Bankipur win, says BJP voters backed him
Prashant Kishor won the Bankipur bypoll and ruled out joining any political alliance in Bihar. The result gives Jan Suraaj its first Assembly seat and sharpens pressure on the BJP-led government.
Jan Suraaj Party founder Prashant Kishor on Monday ruled out joining any political alliance after his victory in the Bankipur Assembly bypoll in Bihar, saying his party's alliance would be with the people of the state.
Kishor defeated BJP's Neeraj Kumar by 18,953 votes in his electoral debut, winning 63,203 votes against Kumar's 44,250. The victory gives Jan Suraaj its first seat in the Bihar Assembly and ends the BJP's run in the constituency, which it had held since 1995.
"We shall have no alliance. Our alliance shall be with the people of Bihar. You should see that the people of Bankipur have voted for us, giving up on established parties," Kishor told reporters after the result.
Asked whether he would reconsider his earlier decision to contest elections without an alliance, Kishor said he would not.
'BJP, CONGRESS, RJD VOTERS BACKED US'
Kishor credited his victory to support from voters and workers who were unhappy with their respective parties, including the BJP, Congress and RJD.
"I would like to thank my active supporters as well as those who backed me in the by-election, despite not being with Jan Suraaj. I received support from people in BJP, Congress and RJD, who were unhappy with the state of affairs in their party," he said.
Kishor had described the Bankipur bypoll as a "referendum" on the BJP-led government in Bihar. He also suggested that the atmosphere created by recent Gen Z protests may have contributed to the result.
"The atmosphere created by Gen Z protests" might have played a role, he said, but added that there was little evidence of a large turnout among young voters in Bankipur.
"There is nothing to show that young electors had voted in large numbers in Bankipur. It is unfortunate, but that is the reality," Kishor said.
Turnout in the July 30 bypoll was below 35 per cent.
KISHOR CALLS RESULT A REJECTION OF SAMRAT CHOUDHARY
Kishor also claimed that the mandate was primarily against Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary.
He said the verdict was a mandate "against whom I have nothing personal, but who is detested by educated people of Bihar because of criminal antecedents and lack of qualifications".
Kishor called the result a wake-up call for Prime Minister Narendra Modi and said that if Choudhary's selection was linked to his Kushwaha caste, he should be replaced by someone from the same community with a "cleaner background".
Choudhary, who joined the BJP less than a decade ago and became the party's first leader to head a government in Bihar, congratulated Kishor in a post on X and described the contest as "the grand festival of democracy".
BJP LEADER BLAMES GROWING DISSATISFACTION
A senior BJP leader attributed the defeat to growing dissatisfaction among the party's traditional upper-caste support base.
"Prashant Kishor struck all the right notes. He tapped into the growing dissatisfaction among the upper castes by raising issues like the death after suspected rape of a NEET aspirant and the police encounter of Bharat Tiwari," the leader said on condition of anonymity.
The leader also said remarks by BJP figures had compounded the problem, referring to Patna Sahib MP Ravi Shankar Prasad's comment that Bankipur was a seat "we can win even if a dog or a cat was fielded as the BJP candidate".
"The Gen Z protests highlighted our weakening support among the youth, especially the upper castes, who have been our core base. They had been unhappy over the controversial UGC regulations and, now, they have begun to feel that we are taking them for granted," the BJP leader said.
OPPOSITION SEES BJP DEFEAT
Leaders of INDIA bloc parties stopped short of congratulating Kishor but described the result as a setback for the BJP.
CPI(ML) Liberation general secretary Dipankar Bhattacharya called it "an emphatic victory against the BJP" and said the result, coming against the backdrop of the Jantar Mantar protests, indicated "a welcome shift in public mood".
Congress spokesperson Suman Kumar Mallick said Bankipur voters had sent a message against "the arrogance of power and autocracy".
"If Parliamentary elections are held today, Modi government will definitely be voted out," he said.
RJD spokesperson Chitaranjan Gagan, whose party candidate Rekha Gupta finished third, said the key point was that the BJP had lost.
"We are not dejected and will work with renewed vigour to ensure the overthrow of the NDA from Bihar as well as the Centre," he said.
Veteran socialist leader Shivanand Tiwary, meanwhile, called on the INDIA bloc to approach Kishor.
"Prashant Kishor's energy and organisational abilities have been there for all to see. The INDIA bloc must approach him. The victory in Bankipur must be viewed in a larger perspective," Tiwary said.
Recalling the student protests, Tiwary said the recent demonstrations at Jantar Mantar, across Bihar and elsewhere were far bigger than the 1974 movement, adding that today's student activists were showing "far superior acumen" than in his time.
JAN SURAaj GETS FIRST ASSEMBLY SEAT
The Bankipur victory marks Jan Suraaj's first electoral success after the party drew a blank in last year's Bihar Assembly election.
Kishor, who gave up political consultancy in 2021, has now entered the Bihar Assembly as an elected representative and secured a victory over a BJP candidate in a constituency the party had held for three decades.
He said he would not make "tall promises" such as turning Bankipur into Bengaluru, but promised to work towards improving the constituency and said changes would be visible within a few months.
The bypoll was necessitated after fifth-term MLA Nitin Nabin resigned from Bankipur following his election to the Rajya Sabha after being elevated as the BJP's national president.
With Jan Suraaj opening its account in the Bihar Assembly, Kishor's first electoral victory has also set the stage for a new political force in the state, even as he maintains that the party will continue to contest without alliances.

headline: India approved just one Chinese FDI proposal worth ₹1 crore, while clearing 13 applications from Hong Kong worth ₹610.42 crore in the last financial year, according to official data.
full_text:
India approved just one Chinese FDI proposal worth ₹1 crore, while clearing 13 applications from Hong Kong worth ₹610.42 crore in the last financial year, according to official data.
These approvals are important as investments from countries sharing a land border with India have been subject to prior government approval since April 2020 under Press Note 3 of the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT).
The measure was introduced to curb opportunistic takeovers and acquisitions of Indian companies during the COVID-19 pandemic.
Overall, the government has approved 63 FDI (foreign direct investment) proposals worth ₹10,292.67 crore, or $1.18 billion, during April 2025-March 2026, according to the DPIIT data.
Singapore emerged as the largest source of approved FDI proposals in value terms, with five proposals worth ₹3,259.88 crore ($382.52 million) receiving clearance.
This was followed by the UK, where five proposals worth ₹2,477.67 crore ($283 million) were approved, and Thailand, which received approval for two proposals worth ₹1,600 crore (about $180 million).
In March, the government eased Press Note 3 of April 2020. Under that, it stated that investors with non-controlling LBC (land border countries) beneficial ownership of up to 10% would be permitted under the automatic route, according to the applicable sectoral caps, entry routes, and other conditions.
However, it was clarified that the relaxed FDI norms will not apply to entities registered in China/Hong Kong or other countries sharing land borders with India.
Countries that share land borders with India are China, Bangladesh, Pakistan, Bhutan, Nepal, Myanmar, and Afghanistan.
India has never received significant investments directly from China. China ranks 23rd, accounting for only 0.32% of total FDI equity inflows into India between April 2000 and March 2026, at $2.51 billion (₹16,162.25 crore).
On the other hand, Hong Kong was at 15th position with only a 0.62% share ($4.91 billion or ₹31,220.30 crore) in the total FDI equity inflow reported during that period.
Like 2025-26, India had approved only one Chinese FDI proposal in 2024-25 also. It was valued at ₹28.71 crore ($3.44 million). In that fiscal, a total of 82 proposals were approved under the government route, involving a total investment of ₹39,758 crore ($4.72 billion).
From Hong Kong, 11 proposals worth ₹1,225.28 crore ($146.51 million) received approval in 2024-25.

headline: 'Bangladesh uprising that was taken over by Jihadis': What CJP protest reminded Taslima Nasreen of

'Bangladesh uprising that was taken over by Jihadis': What CJP protest reminded Taslima Nasreen of
Taslima Nasreen said she was concerned about such movements due to what happened in Bangladesh after the 2024 student protest.
Exiled Bangladeshi author Taslima Nasreen said on Sunday that while she did not follow the student protest at Jantar Mantar, a small clip of it reminded her of the 2024 student uprising in Bangladesh that led to the ouster of then Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina.
She said that the 2024 Bangladesh protests “fooled” people because it looked like the students were protesting against the quota system, it was later found out that “jihadis (Islamic fundamentalists)” were behind it.
"It was like that. That student movement in Bangladesh fooled us. Because we thought the students wanted to abolish the quota system. Sheikh Hasina had also agreed to their demands, but ultimately the government fell. Later, we found that jihadis (Islamic fundamentalists) were behind that movement. The fallout has not been good for Bangladesh. Jihadis have taken over power there," Nasreen was quoted as saying by news agency PTI.

She added that she was concerned about such movements due to what happened in Bangladesh after the 2024 student protest.
‘Want Hasina to return to Bangladesh’
Nasreen also backed ousted former Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, who is in living in exile in India, and said that she was against the ban on her party Awami League back in their home country.
"No political party should be banned. The manner in which Awami League's Sheikh Hasina was forced to leave the country is questionable. It was not right to ban the Awami League. It was a move against democracy," she said.

“I want the ban to be lifted as soon as possible. The party should be allowed to participate in the elections, and I want Hasina to return to Bangladesh,” she added.
Awami League was banned in Bangladesh in 2025 by the country's interim government under anti-terrorism legislation. The author also said that workers of Hasina's party have faced violence in Bangladesh since then.

Nasreen herself was forced to leave Bangladesh in 1994 after she faced death threats from radical religious groups over her writings and religious views. She has been living in exile in India since 2004.
In 2007, she was forced to leave Kolkata as well due to violent protests over her writings.
On Friday, she came back to Kolkata after almost two decades of being forced out of the city. “I can’t believe that I am in Kolkata now. I was driven out in 2007. Initially I had thought that I will be able to return. Kolkata is a progressive city. But as years passed, I had a feeling that I may never be able to return. But then Osman Gani Mallik of Secular Mission invited me to Kolkata. He made all the arrangements,” she said after returning in an interview to a television channel.

headline: Hundreds of students continued their protest for the fifth consecutive day in Ranchi on Sunday (August 2, 2026) over alleged irregularities in the 14th JPSC examination, JSSC-CGL and other recruitment tests, demanding a CBI probe and reforms in the r...
full_text:
Hundreds of students continued their protest for the fifth consecutive day in Ranchi on Sunday (August 2, 2026) over alleged irregularities in the 14th JPSC examination, JSSC-CGL and other recruitment tests, demanding a CBI probe and reforms in the recruitment agencies.
The protesters, who have been holding an indefinite sit-in at a stadium since July 29, raised slogans such as 'Order CBI probe in JPSC', 'Long live Students Unity' and 'Shame on Hemant Soren'.
"Paper leaks in JPSC have happened several times. This time, OMR sheets of candidates have been leaked. Chief Minister Hemant Soren has ordered a CID probe, but we are not satisfied," JPSC aspirant Rahul Kumar Kranti said.
He alleged that previous probes into the Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission (JSSC)-CGL paper leak had not led to action and claimed that the latest investigation could also be "covered up" after a few months.
"We have completely lost faith in the ongoing CID probe. We demand a CBI probe into all recruitment examinations conducted by the JPSC and JSSC over the past seven years. We also demand the chief minister's resignation on moral grounds," Mr. Kranti said.
The protesters are demanding cancellation of the 14th JPSC Combined Preliminary Test held on April 19 and an independent probe by central agencies, including the CBI and Enforcement Directorate (ED), into alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations conducted by the JPSC and JSSC.
They are also demanding the introduction of a fifth option of "not attempted" in OMR sheets.
"The careers of thousands of students and aspirants are at stake due to corruption in both agencies. Most of us come from farmers' families. We only want fair opportunities based on merit," said Ankit Kumar from Giridih district.
Sneha, a tribal student from Ranchi, said protesters wanted strict punishment for those involved in alleged irregularities and cancellation of the 14th JPSC examination.
"I have been preparing for competitive examinations since 2023. But if an equal and fair chance is not given, how can I get a job? I urge CM Soren to listen to our demands," she said.
Archana Kumari from Palamu said the protesters would continue their agitation until the government addressed their demands and fixed accountability for the alleged irregularities.
"The State government is still in a sleeping mode. We are getting support from across the country. People from various cities are sending food items to the protest site. We are thankful to those helping us continue our protest," said Shyam Bihari Gupta, a student from Balumath in Latehar district.
Meanwhile, thousands of students held a torchlight procession in the state capital this evening.
The students, who are holding an indefinite sit-in at the Jaipal Singh Munda stadium, marched to Albert Ekka Chowk. There, they raised slogans against the JMM-led alliance government and demanded an impartial probe into the alleged irregularities in the 14th JPSC, JSCC-CGL and other state-level public recruitment tests.
They said if the state government does not address their concerns, they will march to the Jharkhand Assembly and stage a gherao in the next couple of days.
"We have been holding protests, but no government officials approached us to listen to our concerns on these issues. This clearly shows the insensitivity of this JMM-led alliance government towards the thousands of students and youths of the state," they alleged.

headline: Glaw Lake becomes Arunachal Pradesh's first Ramsar site, India's 101st
full_text:
Glaw Lake becomes Arunachal Pradesh's first Ramsar site, India's 101st
Ramsar sites are wetlands of international importance under the Ramsar Convention, an environmental treaty established in 1971.
The Glaw Lake in Arunachal Pradesh, tucked in the wilderness of Kamlang Tiger Reserve and Wildlife Sanctuary, was designated as the state’s first Ramsar site and the 101st in India, Union Environment Minister Bhupender Yadav announced on Monday.
Ramsar sites are wetlands of international importance under the Ramsar Convention, an environmental treaty established in 1971 to conserve biodiversity, particularly waterfowl habitats.
In a post on X, Yadav said the “pristine freshwater lake in the Eastern Himalayas is a biodiversity hotspot”. “Powered by 101. India continues Her journey beyond a century in designating Ramsar Sites. Delighted to announce Glaw Lake as Arunachal Pradesh’s first Ramsar Site — a significant milestone for biodiversity, water and climate security, and sustainable livelihoods,” he said.
“Fed by perennial mountain streams, it is surrounded by lush vegetation, with more than 150 tree species and 49 orchid species recorded within the site and its catchment,” he added.
The Union Minister also said India has emerged as a global leader in wetland conservation under Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s leadership. “From 26 Ramsar Sites in 2014 to 101 today, this remarkable journey reflects our unwavering commitment to environmental protection, biodiversity conservation, and sustainable development,” he said.
“Every new Ramsar Site strengthens our resolve to protect nature while securing the future of communities that depend on these invaluable ecosystems,” he added.
Ramsar sites are selected based on their international significance in terms of ecology, botany, zoology, limnology or hydrology. Applicant countries designate sites that meet at least one of nine criteria, such as supporting vulnerable species, maintaining biodiversity.
Such sites are also significant as they can serve as model examples of a nation’s commitment to conservation and management under internationally accepted frameworks. In designating a wetland as a Ramsar site, countries agree to establish and oversee a management framework aimed at conserving the wetland.

headline: Bill to provide statutory framework to Indian Statistical Institute introduced in LS
full_text:
Bill to provide statutory framework to Indian Statistical Institute introduced in LS
New Delhi, A bill was introduced in the Lok Sabha on Monday to widen the remit of the Indian Statistical Institute and align its legal framework with evolving needs.
The bill was introduced by Union Minister Rao Indrajit Singh amid opposition protests over the NEET paper leak issue and the alleged theft of donations from the Ram temple in Ayodhya.
Some opposition members, who had given notices to oppose the bill at the introduction stage, did not speak.The bill was then introduced by a voice vote.
The Indian Statistical Institute Bill, 2026, seeks the institute's incorporation as a 'body corporate' to strengthen its governance, promote academic excellence and research and allow it to serve the emerging needs in the field of statistics and allied fields.
The bill says the President of India will be the Visitor of the institute and provisions for a Board of Governors that will be its principal policy executive body.
The board will be headed by the chairperson, who will be an eminent person from the field of academia, industry, education, public policy, and statistical sciences.
The board will be accountable to the central government, the bill notes.
The institute will have an Academic Council, which will act as its principal academic body and will be headed by the institute's director.
All full-time professors and full-time faculty will be members of the Academic Council.
The Indian Statistical Institute Act, 1959, declared the institute to be an institution of national importance and empowered it to grant degrees and diplomas in statistics.
The Act was amended in 1995 to empower the Institute to grant degrees and diplomas in statistics, mathematics, quantitative economics, computer science and such other subjects related to statistics as may be determined by it from time to time.
The 1959 Act, according to the bill, has limited provisions in respect of the governance, administration, finance, accountability and functioning of the Institute and is not adequate to enable it to respond to the requirements of an evolving academic and research environment.
Therefore, it says, the government decided to repeal the Indian Statistical Institute Act, 1959, to bring out comprehensive legislation providing for the incorporation of the Indian Statistical Institute, an institution of national importance, to excel as a globally recognised centre in Statistical Sciences and allied fields.
The legal reform will enable an ecosystem to train a new generation of high-quality data scientists and statisticians, bridging the massive talent gap currently facing India's tech and financial sectors, the bill says.

'If even one allegation was proved...': Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh reacts after acquittal in wrestlers' sexual harassment
Former Wrestling Federation of India (WFI) chief Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh welcomed his acquittal in the sexual harassment case.
Former Wrestling Federation of India (WFI) chief Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh welcomed his acquittal in the sexual harassment case filed by six women wrestlers, saying the verdict vindicated the stand he had maintained since the allegations first surfaced.
“The honourable judge said that Brij Bhushan Singh and Vinod Tomar are acquitted with honour. From the very first day, I had said that if even a single allegation against me was proved, I would be ready to face the harshest punishment,” he said.
“Today, the court has acquitted us with honour and it is a matter of happiness for me. What I had said on the first day has turned out to be true. I did not know what the other side was thinking, but my first reaction was that the truth would prevail. Today is a moment of happiness.”
‘Matter of joy for me and supporters’: Brij Bhushan
"On the first day, when my first statement came, I had said that if any verdict or any charge is proven, I will hang myself. Today, the court acquitted me with honour. It is a matter of joy for me and my supporters... Today is a happy day," Singh said.
A Delhi court on Monday acquitted Singh and former WFI assistant secretary Vinod Tomar in the case, bringing to an end a trial that began nearly two years ago.
Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate (CJM) Ashwini Panwar of the Rouse Avenue Courts had reserved the judgment on July 2 after directing both the prosecution and the defence to submit their written arguments within two weeks.
Singh had been charged under Sections 354 (assault or criminal force to a woman with intent to outrage her modesty), 354A (sexual harassment) and 506(1) (criminal intimidation) of the Indian Penal Code (IPC). Tomar was charged with criminal intimidation. The offences carry a maximum punishment of five years' imprisonment.

What was the case?
The case stemmed from allegations made by six women wrestlers, who accused Singh of sexually harassing multiple female athletes over several years. Their accusations sparked months-long protests at Delhi's Jantar Mantar in 2023, with the wrestlers demanding Singh's arrest and removal as WFI chief.
Singh, then a Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) MP from Uttar Pradesh's Kaiserganj, was removed from the top post in the federation following the allegations. Tomar, a close aide of Singh and the WFI's assistant secretary, was also suspended.
The protests were briefly called off after the Union Sports Ministry assured the wrestlers that a committee would investigate the allegations. However, they resumed in April 2023 after the athletes alleged that no meaningful action had been taken.

headline: A seat for JSP's 'school bag': Why Prashant Kishor's Bankipur win is a warning for both BJP and RJD
full_text:
A seat for JSP's 'school bag': Why Prashant Kishor's Bankipur win is a warning for both BJP and RJD
Kunal Varma / TIMESOFINDIA.COM / Updated: Aug 04, 2026, 07:54 IST
Comments
Share
AA
Text Size
Small

Large
Prashant Kishor celebrates after winning the Bankipur Assembly bypoll (Image credit: PTI)
NEW DELHI: Jan Suraaj Party (JSP) founder Prashant Kishor has finally found a seat for his âschool bagâ in Bihar. The election strategist-turned-politician, whose party contests on a school bag symbol, has flipped the Bankipur assembly seat, an unassailable bastion of the BJP for the last 30 years. Before todayâs shock defeat, the BJP had registered 8 consecutive victories in Bankipur since 1995, when it won the seat for the first time.By-election in Bankipur was necessitated after Nitin Nabin resigned as BJP MLA from the seat in April after his election to Rajya Sabha. This followed Nitin Nabinâs elevation as BJP national president in January this year.To gauge the enormity of Prashant Kishorâs victory, look at these facts:
BJP has held Bankipur assembly seat from 1995 (Till 2005, the seat was known as Patna West)
BJP chief Nitin Nabin won from the Bankipur assembly seat four times in a row
Nitin Nabin won from Bankipur for first time in 2010 with a margin of 56%
From 1995 to 2010, the seat (known as Patna West) was represented by Navin Kishore Prasad Sinha (Nitin Nabinâs father)
Father-son duo has won the seat 8 consecutive times
For PK, as Prashant Kishor is popularly known, contesting the Bankipur byelection was a huge political gamble. PK, who made a high-pitched entry into Bihar politics with a padyatra spanning months ahead of the 2025 assembly elections, cut a sorry figure when his Jan Suraj Party failed to win even one seat less than a year ago. Such dismal was his first electoral show that JSP lost deposit in 236 of the 238 seats it contested. Prashant Kishor did not contest the election himself and instead led a high-voltage campaign for his party across the state.
Little wonder his decision to contest the Bankipur bypoll was fraught with the danger of becoming a make-or-break political move. But the gamble has paid off and Prashant Kishor with his debut win has propelled into the centrestage of Bihar politics.
âBankipurâs message to BJP central leadershipâ
Prashant Kishor polled over 64,151 votes and won the key electoral battle by a margin of 19,324 votes over BJPâs Neeraj Kumar. Prashant Kishorâs resounding success, nine months after his partyâs humiliating defeat, marks a remarkable turnaround.And making the most of his victory, Prashant Kishor immediately trained his guns at Bihar chief minister Samrat Choudhary."This is the victory of the people of Bankipur. As we stated during the election campaign, this was not just an election to choose an MLA. It was an attempt by the people of Bihar to send a message to the BJP's central leadership that they should appoint a good person as the chief minister of Bihar. They do not want a person with a criminal background or questionable conduct, character, or reputation to lead Bihar. They want a good chief minister who can improve education, create employment opportunities for the youth, and ensure that the children of Bihar do not have to migrate elsewhere for work," Kishor told reporters as his supporters celebrated his maiden electoral victory.
Prashant Kishor hits out at Bihar CM
Prashant Kishorâs use of his victory to target Samrat Choudhary did not come as a surprise. Ksihor been unrelenting in his attacks against the BJP leader ever since the election strategist became a full-time politician. He has targeted Samrat Choudhary over the chief ministerâs educational qualification and his alleged criminal past.
Kishor's development pitch or disappointment against BJP?
The Jan Suraaj chief also called upon the BJP's central leadership to focus on governance ahead of the next Lok Sabha elections, stating, "Before the Lok Sabha elections, Prime Minister Modi, the BJP, and Amit Shah should focus on improving Bihar, creating jobs for its youth, and stopping migration. That is our only objective. We do not want to become MLAs merely to award contracts. Our sole objective is the development of Bihar."These are the very themes on which Prashant Kishor fought the 2025 assembly elections and lost. Clearly, while he keeps focus on these issues, his victory in bankipur may less be about endorsement of his development focus and more about peopleâs disappointment with the BJP. The result is also perhaps a fallout of the studentsâ agitation against NEET-UG paper leak, which saw huge protests in Bihar. In Siwan, a police constable was suspended after a video purportedly showing him using an AK-47 rifle during a student protest on July 25 went viral on social media.Leader of opposition in Bihar assembly, Tejashwi Yadav, slammed Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary for the incident. He posted a video of the purported incident on X and, along with it, said, "During the protest in Siwan, police resorted to direct firing with an AK-47 on students. When a criminal becomes chief minister, then police fire bullets at innocent students.â
âVerdict by Bihar's youth against BJPâ
CPI(ML) Liberation general secretary Dipankar Bhattacharya in his message to Prashant Kishor described his victory as a significant verdict by Bihar's youth against the BJP-led state government.In a post on X, Bhattacharya termed Kishor's victory a "well-earned debut victory" and said the bypoll result reflected public anger against the ruling dispensation."Congratulations to Prashant Kishor on his well-earned debut victory in Bankipur bypoll. Kudos to the youth of Bihar for delivering such a telling blow to the supremely arrogant, incompetent and tyrannical BJP government of Bihar," he said.
Shock verdict for BJP
The BJP was quick to accept the verdict of the people. State BJP president Sanjay Saraogi said in a statement, "We bow before the will of the people. We shall draw lessons from the debacle, unlike our opponents who tend to blame every electoral loss of theirs on EVMs and the Election Commission".But for the BJP, this defeat comes as an embarrassment for both its national president Nitin Nabin and the partyâs first chief minister in the state Samrat Choudhary. Bankipur seat was literally a personal fiefdom of Nitin Nabinâs family which represented the constituency for 30 long years. A defeat in the backyard will surely embarrass the BJP chief.For Samrat Choudhary, this was the first electoral test of his government which was formed after the BJP took over the reins of the state from JD(U) chief Nitish Kumar. It was Nitish Kumar who had led the NDA to an emphatic triumph in the 2025 assembly elections. And the BJP would have hoped that Samrat Choudhary would have given it a winning start. But that was not to be.
Lalu's RJD pushed to fringes
The Bankipur bypoll result also has a worrying message for the main opposition party RJD. Tejashwi Yadavâs party seems to have learnt no lessons from the 2025 electoral drubbing. The party which has been reduced to 25 seats in the assembly did little to show intent on the ground.
Its candidate Rekha Kumari polled just 14,273 votes. This was over 32,000 votes less than the figure of 46,363, which she had polled in the 2025 assembly elections as the runnerup in the seat. Ironically, for the greater part of the campaign, RJDâs star campaigner Tejashwi Yadav was missing in action.
Time to pause, review
It may not be prudent to overexaggerate the outcome of one bypoll. The result of one seat, even though high-profile, may not be indicative of any larger trend. But for the BJP and the RJD to brush aside the defeat as a one-off setback would be doing harm to their cause. The BJP should remember that it rules Bihar but is still dependent on its allies for survival. The RJD, meanwhile, remains the main opposition party but seems to have lost the plot to factionalism and family feuds after its dismal 2025 show. Both need to pause and review what went wrong in Bankipur. MLA Prashant Kishor, on the other hand, will perhaps be now preparing for another bout with his political bete noir Samrat Choudhary - this time on the floor of Bihar assembly.

headline: The Lok Sabha on Monday (August 3, 2026) passed a Bill to increase the sanctioned strength of judges in the Supreme Court without any discussion as persistent protests by Opposition members over the police action against protesting students at Jantar...
full_text:
The Lok Sabha on Monday (August 3, 2026) passed a Bill to increase the sanctioned strength of judges in the Supreme Court without any discussion as persistent protests by Opposition members over the police action against protesting students at Jantar Mantar and the alleged chadhawa chori (theft of offerings) at the Ram Temple in Ayodhya continued to disrupt proceedings.
Two other legislations — the Bankers’ Books Evidence Bill, 2026, and the Indian Statistical Institute Bill, 2026 — were introduced amid sloganeering in the afternoon.
Parliament Monsoon Session Day 11 highlights
The House was adjourned repeatedly during the day as Opposition members trooped into the Well raising slogans and displaying placards, forcing Speaker Om Birla to suspend proceedings first till noon, then till 2 p.m., before adjourning the House for the day following the passage of the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Bill, 2026.
At the Business Advisory Committee (BAC) meeting, sources told The Hindu that Congress deputy leader Gaurav Gogoi, Chief Whip Kodikunnil Suresh and Samajwadi Party MP Dharmendra Yadav demanded that Home Minister Amit Shah make a statement in the House on the police crackdown on protesters and that the government initiate a discussion on the alleged embezzlement of funds at the Ram Temple in Ayodhya, during which Prime Minister Narendra Modi could intervene.
The BAC allotted three hours each for discussion on the Bankers’ Books Evidence Bill and the Indian Statistical Institute Bill, and five hours for the Taxation and Other Laws (Amendment) Bill. However, there was no discussion on taking up the proposed amendments to the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act (FCRA).
The Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Bill replaces an ordinance promulgated earlier this year to raise the sanctioned strength of the apex court from 34 to 38 judges, including the Chief Justice of India. A statutory resolution moved by Opposition members seeking disapproval of the ordinance was rejected by voice vote.
Union Law Minister Arjun Ram Meghwal briefly introduced the Bill, but with protests continuing, it was passed by voice vote without debate. The government has argued that increasing the court’s strength is essential to address mounting pendency. As of January 1, the Supreme Court had 92,101 pending cases. The legislation says the additional judges would also enable the Chief Justice of India to constitute Constitution Benches more regularly. Five judges have already been appointed following the promulgation of the ordinance.
Amid the disruptions, the House also introduced the Indian Statistical Institute Bill, 2026, and the Bankers’ Books Evidence Bill, 2026.
The Indian Statistical Institute Bill seeks to repeal the 1959 Act governing the institution and incorporate it as a statutory body corporate with the President as its Visitor and a Board of Governors as its principal executive body. It also provides for an Academic Council headed by the Director to strengthen governance, research and academic autonomy while expanding the institute’s role in statistics, data science and allied disciplines.
The Bankers’ Books Evidence Bill, introduced by Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman, seeks to replace the colonial-era 1891 law by recognising electronic, digital, virtual and cloud-based banking records as admissible evidence in courts. It also provides for digital authentication of records and empowers the Centre to extend the law to other financial sector entities. Both Bills were introduced by voice vote after Opposition members who had submitted notices opposing their introduction did not press their objections.

headline: Karnataka rules out Cauvery bandh, DK Shivakumar says state will protect interests
full_text:
Karnataka rules out Cauvery bandh, DK Shivakumar says state will protect interests
After an all-party meeting, DK Shivakumar urged parties and Kannada groups not to call a bandh over the Cauvery dispute. He said Karnataka would protect its interests through legal channels while prioritising drinking water amid a sharp rainfall deficit.
Karnataka Chief Minister DK Shivakumar on Sunday urged political parties and Kannada organisations not to call for a bandh over the Cauvery water-sharing dispute, asserting that protecting Karnataka's interests would remain the government's top priority.
Speaking after an all-party meeting convened to discuss directions issued by the Cauvery Water Management Authority (CWMA) and the Cauvery Water Regulation Committee (CWRC), Shivakumar said the government would act strictly within the legal framework while safeguarding the state's interests.
He said the CWMA and the CWRC had directed Karnataka to release 3,500 cusecs of water to Tamil Nadu, but stressed that the state was facing a severe rainfall deficit, having received only around 35 per cent of its normal rainfall so far this year.
The Chief Minister said ensuring drinking water remained the government's immediate priority. Water was being released through canals only to fill lakes and tanks meant for drinking water, not for irrigation, while district-wise crop advisories would be issued based on water availability.
Shivakumar said Karnataka had released only around 3.6 TMC of water in July this year compared with about 31 TMC during the same period last year because of poor inflows. Improved rainfall in recent days had marginally eased the situation, with Kabini reaching full capacity and inflows into reservoirs increasing.
He appealed to the BJP, JD(S) and Kannada organisations to maintain unity and avoid a bandh, saying all parties had agreed during the all-party meeting to support the government's stand on the issue.
Shivakumar said Karnataka would continue consultations with legal experts and pursue its case before the courts. He added that the state had sought cooperation from Tamil Nadu on ensuring drinking water needs and would continue discussions through legal and administrative channels.
The Chief Minister also said he had requested an appointment with Prime Minister Narendra Modi for an all-party delegation to present Karnataka's concerns. According to Shivakumar, the Prime Minister responded positively and said he would convey a suitable time for the meeting.
Calling the proposed Mekedatu balancing reservoir project the permanent solution to the Cauvery dispute, Shivakumar said the Detailed Project Report faced only minor documentation issues and reiterated that 9 TMC of water under the project had been earmarked exclusively for drinking water.
On possible compensation if farmers are advised against cultivation, Shivakumar said the Revenue Minister was examining the issue and an appropriate decision would be taken at the right time. Asked about Cabinet expansion, he declined to confirm a timeline, saying the media would be informed before any decision was taken.

headline: After days of deliberations and lobbying, the much-awaited Cabinet expansion is likely to take place on Monday evening with the Karnataka government learnt to have informally sought time from Governor Thaawarchand Gehlot for the swearing-in of new Mi...
full_text:
After days of deliberations and lobbying, the much-awaited Cabinet expansion is likely to take place on Monday evening with the Karnataka government learnt to have informally sought time from Governor Thaawarchand Gehlot for the swearing-in of new Ministers at Lok Bhavan.
While the list containing names of the legislators to be sworn in is expected to reach Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar on Monday morning from the Congress Central leadership, party sources said that many of the chosen legislators could be intimated soon after the list arrives.
Sources said that though the Central leadership had preferred Saturday for the swearing-in with the list being ready, it had been postponed for an ‘astrologically favourable day’, which happens to be Monday. “Informally, the government has sought time between 4 p.m. and 6 p.m. on Monday from the Governor,” sources said.
On Sunday, when presspersons asked Mr. Shivakumar about the absence of the Governor in Bengaluru, he said that Mr. Gehlot will be returning on Monday.
Sources said that speculation about who would be lucky to enter the Cabinet has been doing the rounds, but the leaders have been tight-lipped over the names. “The lists carried by Mr. Shivakumar and former Chief Minister Siddaramaiah are believed to have undergone changes as the party is looking to bring in a balance.”
The party is walking a tightrope with over 50 legislators aspiring to be Ministers, and its decision has to take into account regional, caste and community equations. “One of the important criteria has been the winnable factor in the next elections and their influence in their region to help other party candidates win in the 2028 elections,” sources said.
Sources said that competition is intense among Muslim legislators from Bengaluru that has turned out to be a stress point with elections to five corporations in Greater Bengaluru Authority region expected to be held shortly. “Similarly, with the KPCC president post going to B.K. Hariprasad, an OBC, demand for a higher share for Lingayats has emerged and there are many competing forces within the community. Some senior legislators are also lobbying for the post of the Speaker.”
The list has been drawn considering the post of the Chairman and the Deputy Chairman of the Legislative Council, sources added.

headline: Opposition parties on Monday (August 3, 2026) continued to protest in the Parliament House complex against the alleged donation theft at the Ram Temple in Ayodhya and police crackdown on the anti-paper leak student demonstrations on July 20.

Like last week, the MPs kept donation boxes near the Parliament entrance, ‘Makar Dwar’, to symbolise the alleged theft of donations at the temple and lined up around them to raise slogans against the government. Some MPs put cash in the box enacting the donations made and the “theft” that took place later.
Members of the Samajwadi Party who were present said till now more than ₹47,000 has been collected and the money would be donated to the Ram Temple at Ayodhya and a receipt would be taken.
The MPs had staged a similar skit last week, which had led to objections from Hindu outfits and the BJP who alleged that it was an insult to ‘Sanatan Dharma’.

Congress’ Priyanka Gandhi, SP’s Dimple Yadav and Dharmendra Yadav, Trinamool Congress’ Mahua Moitra, Jarkhand Mukti Morcha’s Mahua Maji, Revolutionary Socialist Party’s N.K. Premachandran, were among those who were seen at the protest.

full_text: New Delhi: There is no official word on the Narendra Modi government on bringing a fresh Bill to amend the Constitution to carry out a delimitation but if it does so, all eyes will be on the DMK with 22 members in the Lok Sabha and eight in the Rajya Sabha.While it will be a bit easier for the BJP-led NDA to get the contentious proposal through in the Rajya Sabha where it is closer to two-thirds majority, the ruling side will find it difficult to gather numbers to cross the hurdle in the Lok Sabha.After its exit from the I.N.D.I.A. bloc over the "betrayal" by the Congress which has gone with Vijay's TVK in Tamil Nadu, the DMK has so far not given any clear indication of supporting the Bill though it has been insisting that it would make up its mind only after examining the new Bill..Supporting Delimitation Bill amounts to betraying people of Tamil Nadu: Rahul Gandhi tells DMK.DMK leaders maintain that they may not be working in tandem with the Congress but are not leaving the Opposition space and cited how they opposed the bill on Vande Mataram and the one on paper leak by moving amendments and voting against it. The party is also set to oppose the Foreign Contribution Regulation Amendment Bill whenever it comes to the House.. I.N.D.I.A. bloc parties also express hope that the DMK will not vote in favour of the delimitation bill with its chief M K Stalin having burnt a copy of the bill as a symbolic protest. Upping the ante, Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi said anybody supporting the delimitation bill would be a 21st century ‘Ettappan’, drawing a parallel with the 18th century Tamil ruler who allegedly aided the British against Veerapandiya Kattabomman.If all 540 sitting members — three seats are vacant — of the Lok Sabha vote, the bill would require 360 votes, which is the two-thirds required for its passage. The NDA has 319 MPs now with the addition to 20 rebel Trinamool Congress MPs and six who crossed over from the Shiv Sena (UBT) to Shiv Sena.The NDA could be confident of another five votes, including those from the YSR Congress, who voted in favour of the bill in April when it got 298. The NDA had 293 MPs, excluding Speaker Om Birla who won as a BJP candidate, then..'Our support will depend on issues': DMK ready to back Delimitation Bill if its concerns are addressed.If the DMK decides to side with the government on the delimitation Bill, the NDA tally will rise to 346, requiring another 14 to bridge the gap. In case the DMK decides to walkout, the number of MPs voting — if all are present and voting — will come down to 518 and the two-thirds mark would be 345. In such a scenario, the NDA would have to woo 21 more MPs to its side. In the Rajya Sabha, the NDA has 154 members on its side and can get four YSR Congress MPs' support, which would mean it would be short of just six votes to cross two-thirds mark.

headline: Bengaluru: The outpouring of dissent within Karnataka’s ruling Congress over the latest Cabinet expansion spilled into a second straight day Tuesday, with several senior and prominent leaders blaming infighting among top leaders and even the party hi...
full_text:
Bengaluru: The outpouring of dissent within Karnataka’s ruling Congress over the latest Cabinet expansion spilled into a second straight day Tuesday, with several senior and prominent leaders blaming infighting among top leaders and even the party high command for their exclusion from D.K. Shivakumar’s cabinet.
So far, at least one senior Congress legislator has resigned, and several others have indicated that their supporters are pressuring them to follow suit, compounding the challenges for Shivakumar, who himself was made the chief minister in June in place of Siddaramaiah after months of infighting.
“I was close to Siddaramaiah and respect him a great deal even today. But I never liked the behaviour of some people, the way they talk,” M.C. Sudhakar, the Congress legislator from Chikballapura, told Public TV.
The former minister for higher education said that he was “targeted” due to his proximity to Siddaramaiah—who heads one of the three main factions in the Congress party.
People aware of the developments say that after being replaced by Shivakuma as CM, Siddaramaiah nursed a feeling of neglect over the high command’s decision to drop his former colleagues and even stayed away from the 3 August swearing-in ceremony for 19 newly inducted ministers.
Legislators even trained their guns at the All India Congress Committee (AICC) leadership who took two months to draft the cabinet expansion list that threw up many surprises and dropped several seniors without intimation.
“If this process was done quickly, would so many people be upset? They dragged it on for two months and probably the high command did not take Karnataka seriously and did not deal with the situation properly,” Sudhakar said.
Senior legislators like T.B. Jayachandra, Dinesh Gundu Rao, Belur Srinivas, Rahim Khan, Tanveer Said and several others questioned the criteria used to finalise the list.
Jayachandra, one of the senior most party leaders, criticised the decision to include people who entered the party in recent years. “It no longer looks like a Congress government but an all-party government.”
While dissent is not unusual after cabinet expansion exercises, it is bogging the CM down at a time when the state approaches crucial local elections. The severe drought condition also needs urgent government attention.
The state also goes to the polls in 2028, leaving little time for Shivakumar to not just put his own house in order but to overcome growing challenges of fund crunch, fix infrastructure issues, and deliver on effective governance to help retain power.
Shivakumar now faces a daunting task of assuaging tempers, placating disgruntled leaders, managing expectations of the population and putting up a united front to ward off attacks by the Opposition on the streets and the upcoming monsoon session of the state legislature.
‘Injustice has been done’
The Congress high command took two months to finalise the cabinet expansion list largely due to pressure from multiple factions headed by leaders like Shivakumar, Siddararamaiah, and AICC President Mallikarjun Kharge.
Shivakumar and Siddaramaiah spent significant time in Delhi lobbying to secure cabinet berths for their respective loyalists, while several legislators also camped there for weeks to make their case before the high command.
There were changes made to the final list as well: S.S. Mallikarjun replaced Mankal Vaidya and Gayatri Shanthegowda, the lone woman on the list, was not even allowed to take oath.
“Shanthegowda’s name came from the high command as they wanted to accommodate a lady. So, the former CM (Siddaramaiah) suggested Shanthegowda’s name. But then again, her win was legitimised only last Friday and everyone felt that her selection would not be right because there were already two Kurubas (Yathindra Siddaramaiah and Byrathi Suresh) already ministers,” said one cabinet minister of Karnataka, requesting anonymity.
With Shanthegowda excluded, the current cabinet consists of 33 men and no women. Supporters of former minister Lakshmi Hebbalkar, who have been protesting since Monday afternoon, are now hoping for her reinstatement.
Other women leaders including Nayana Motamma, Annapoorna Tukaram and Kaneez Fathima have also demanded to be considered for the last remaining cabinet seat.
Meanwhile, supporters of senior Congress leader M. Krishnappa and his son, MLA Priya Krishna, stormed into the party office in Bengaluru, threatening to resign en masse over the exclusion of their leader(s).
“I don’t deny that injustice has been done. But we will try and placate him elsewhere,” B.K. Hariprasad, the president of the Karnataka Pradesh Congress Committee (KPCC), told protestors Tuesday.
He requested them to not think about resigning, assuring that Priya Krishna still has a lot of politics ahead of him.
‘Will accept resignations’
S.R. Srinivas, the Congress legislator from Gubbi in Tumakuru, said that he cannot do much about being excluded from the cabinet. “It’s difficult for a farmer’s son to rise in politics. You either need a godfather, have earned money dubiously or learnt other skills. This (exclusion) proves these points once again,” Srinivas told reporters Tuesday.
Rao, a six-time MLA from Gandhi Nagar in Bengaluru, said that he was disappointed at being given no reason for his exclusion.
“I am pained not for missing out on a cabinet berth but because I have been given no reason for being dropped,” Rao said.
He also said that it was the first time that a Brahmin would not be part of the state cabinet. Rao had served as the minister for health & family welfare in the previous Siddaramaiah government.
The Chief Minister Tuesday said that he will meet disgruntled MLAs and give them assignments in Boards and Corporations, and assign other roles within the government and party.
Shivakumar said that tendering resignations is common in politics and that he cannot stop anyone from doing so.
He reiterated his own exclusion from the cabinets of Dharam Singh and the earlier Siddaramaiah government (2013-18) and how patience was key to longevity in politics. “The Party is very important. If anyone resigns, within a few minutes I am going to accept it,” Shivakumar said, issuing a stern warning to those threatening to resign.
(Edited by Ajeet Tiwari)

headline: No insurance, no fuel? Supreme Court proposes pilot project at petrol pumps
full_text:
No insurance, no fuel? Supreme Court proposes pilot project at petrol pumps
A major road safety push could make insurance checks routine at fuel stations, while ANPR cameras, police apps and longer insurance cover for new vehicles are also proposed.
The Supreme Court has proposed a major crackdown on vehicles being driven without valid insurance, asking the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) and the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways to prepare a pilot project that could see petrol pumps check a vehicle's insurance before supplying fuel.
Under the proposed system, vehicles without valid insurance could be denied petrol or diesel until the required cover is obtained.
The move is part of a wider set of road safety measures proposed by the court, including linking automatic number plate recognition (ANPR) cameras with vehicle and insurance databases, giving traffic police mobile tools to check insurance instantly and extending the mandatory third-party insurance period for newly purchased vehicles.
NO INSURANCE, NO FUEL PILOT
The court has asked IRDAI and the road transport ministry to work on a pilot project that would allow petrol pumps to verify whether a vehicle has valid insurance before dispensing fuel.
If the vehicle is found to be uninsured, the proposed system could allow fuel stations to refuse the supply of petrol or diesel.
The measure is aimed at increasing compliance with mandatory motor insurance rules and making it harder for uninsured vehicles to remain on the roads.
The proposal is a pilot project and does not mean that petrol pumps across the country will immediately start refusing fuel to uninsured vehicles.
ANPR CAMERAS TO BE LINKED TO INSURANCE DATA
The Supreme Court has also proposed linking ANPR cameras installed on highways and roads with the VAHAN vehicle database and insurance databases.
The system could automatically identify vehicles without valid insurance and generate e-challans against them.
ANPR cameras are already used in several places to detect traffic violations such as speeding, jumping red lights and driving on the wrong side of the road. Linking them with insurance records could extend their use to identifying uninsured vehicles.
POLICE TO GET MOBILE INSURANCE CHECKS
Traffic police could also be provided with mobile applications or handheld devices to check a vehicle's insurance status instantly during roadside inspections.
The proposed devices would be linked to relevant vehicle and insurance databases, allowing officers to verify whether a vehicle has valid cover without relying on physical insurance documents.
LONGER INSURANCE COVER FOR NEW VEHICLES
The court has also proposed extending the mandatory third-party insurance period for newly purchased vehicles.
For new private cars, the compulsory third-party insurance period would increase from three years to four years.
For new two-wheelers, the period would rise from five years to six years.
The move is aimed at reducing the number of vehicles that become uninsured after their initial insurance period expires.
WHY THE COURT IS PUSHING FOR TIGHTER CHECKS
The court has taken a wider view of the problem of uninsured vehicles, with the proposed measures aimed at ensuring that mandatory third-party insurance requirements are actually followed.
The proposed fuel check, ANPR integration and police verification system would create multiple points at which an uninsured vehicle could be identified.
The measures would also make it easier for authorities to track vehicles that continue to operate without the legally required insurance.
The Supreme Court's proposals are now to be worked out by the concerned authorities, with the pilot project expected to examine how the insurance verification system can be implemented without disrupting the functioning of fuel stations or legitimate vehicle use.
For now, the proposals signal a significant tightening of India's approach to uninsured vehicles, with the court looking beyond conventional roadside enforcement towards technology and everyday services such as fuel purchases to improve compliance.

headline: Supreme Court proposes no fuel for uninsured vehicles, seeks Centre's plan
full_text:
Supreme Court proposes no fuel for uninsured vehicles, seeks Centre's plan
The top court also ordered a technology-driven enforcement mechanism to automatically identify and penalise such vehicles without an insurance.
The Supreme Court on Tuesday directed the Centre and the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) to evolve a pilot project under which uninsured vehicles could be denied fuel at petrol pumps, while also ordering a technology-driven enforcement mechanism to automatically identify and penalise such vehicles.
In a landmark bid to tackle the menace of uninsured vehicles and ensure timely compensation for road accident victims, a bench of justice Sanjay Karol and Prashant Kumar Mishra issued a slew of directions, including integration of Automatic Number Plate Recognition (ANPR) cameras with insurance databases to generate automatic e-challans for uninsured vehicles, provision of handheld devices to traffic police for real-time verification of insurance status, enhancement of mandatory third-party insurance tenure for new vehicles, and expeditious disposal of old motor accident compensation cases.
Observing that nearly 56% of vehicles plying on Indian roads remain uninsured, the bench said that the statutory safeguard of compensating road accident victims was often “delayed, if not defeated”, forcing victims and their families into prolonged litigation.
Also Read | Insurer not liable to pay compensation for accidents if driver's licence invalid, says SC
“The object behind mandatory insurance under Section 146 of the Motor Vehicles Act is not just that victims of road accidents are compensated, it is also that they are not drawn into prolonged litigation,” it noted.
The court directed the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) and IRDAI to examine a pilot project under which fuel supply would be linked to a vehicle’s insurance status. “In the absence thereof, the vehicle concerned would be refused fuel at petrol pumps until such time that valid insurance is obtained,” ordered the bench, noting that the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas had, in principle, expressed no objection to the proposal.
Also Read | Time restrictions on filing insurance claims are void: HC
The bench underlined that such a mechanism would help identify uninsured and unregistered vehicles while nudging owners to maintain valid insurance. It suggested that the project could be implemented using ANPR cameras.
To strengthen enforcement, the court directed that ANPR cameras already deployed on highways and city roads for detecting traffic violations be integrated with the Insurance Information Bureau database and the VAHAN portal to enable automatic issuance of e-challans to uninsured vehicles. It also directed States to equip traffic police with handheld devices or mobile applications linked to these databases to verify insurance status on the spot and issue challans.
The court further directed strict implementation of the proposed amendment to Section 196 of the Motor Vehicles Act, which prescribes steeper penalties for driving uninsured vehicles once notified by the Centre.
Also Read | Insurers can deny claim over hiding drinking habit, says SC
In a significant change affecting new vehicle buyers, the bench directed that the mandatory third-party insurance cover be enhanced from three years to four years for new private cars and from five years to six years for new two-wheelers. The court said it was extending the period by one year despite IRDAI and the General Insurance Council recommending against such a move, holding that the measure was necessary in the interest of road safety.
The direction builds upon the Supreme Court’s ruling in S Rajaseekaran Vs Union of India (2018), which had mandated long-term third-party insurance at the time of registration of new vehicles.
The judgment also overhauls the structure of motor insurance policies. Accepting IRDAI’s proposal, the court directed implementation of a uniform four-layer framework comprising a mandatory third-party policy, an optional legal liability cover for occupants and pillion riders, an optional personal accident cover for the owner, driver and occupants, and an optional own-damage cover.
Also Read | Better ride quality, lower fuel average: Nitin Gadkari to Parliament on how E20 petrol affects vehicles
With a view to ensure informed consumer choice, every purchaser of motor insurance -- online or offline, will have to be provided with a standardised customer option form allowing them to opt into additional covers, along with a consumer-friendly information sheet explaining the mandatory and optional components of motor insurance. The court also directed IRDAI, in consultation with the General Insurance Council and insurers, to formulate uniform policy wordings for the optional covers while allowing insurers flexibility in pricing and innovation.
The bench additionally directed insurance companies to prominently display the benefits of comprehensive motor insurance policies on their websites in an easy-to-understand format.
Concerned over delays in compensation cases, the court further revived earlier directions governing motor accident claims for accidents that occurred before March 31, 2022, when the Detailed Accident Report (DAR) regime became operational under the Central Motor Vehicles Rules.
Also Read | Union cabinet approves scheme to replace old trucks, buses to curb air pollution
Relying on a clutch of previous rulings, the bench directed State police to promptly file DARs along with all relevant documents before motor accident claims tribunals (MACTs) in pending pre-March 2022 cases and ensure production of witnesses to facilitate speedy disposal.
The court noted that more than half of MACT cases continue to remain pending for over four years and stressed that road safety forms an integral part of the right to life under Article 21.
The bench directed all stakeholders to comply with its directions and file affidavits by August 14, and listed the matter for monitoring compliance on August 18.
The directions came while disposing of an appeal filed by National Insurance Company Ltd against a Telangana High Court judgment awarding compensation to the family of a man who died in a 1996 road accident while travelling in his own Maruti 800 car. The insurer had argued that the comprehensive insurance policy did not cover the owner’s risk. Affirming the high court’s view, the bench held that a comprehensive policy covered the owner travelling in the vehicle and declined to interfere, reiterating that courts should not adopt a hyper-technical approach in motor accident compensation matters.

headline: Pakistan responded to PoK discontent with bullets, blackouts and repression: MEA
full_text:
Pakistan responded to PoK discontent with bullets, blackouts and repression: MEA
India condemned Pakistan for using lethal force against protesters in PoK, urging global accountability for 90 civilian deaths amid ongoing violence.
India on Tuesday accused Pakistan of using lethal force, intimidation and repression against protesters in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (PoK), resulting in the death of 90 civilians, as it again urged the world community to hold Islamabad accountable for the human rights violations and atrocities.
The remarks by external affairs ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal at a regular media briefing came against the backdrop of Pakistani authorities holding elections in two constituencies in PoK to complete the second phase of polls to the local assembly.
Jaiswal, who was responding to a question on violence by Pakistani security forces against the protesters and the elections to the assembly in PoK, described the electoral exercise as a “complete farce” and called on the world community to focus on “wanton killings” in the region.
“This so-called local election in PoK is a complete farce. The real happening is that of public protests and wanton killings by the Pakistani forces. Such hollow exercises cannot hide reality,” he said.
Jaiswal pointed out that at least 90 civilians had lost their lives in a continuing crackdown by Pakistani authorities since June. “Many more have been injured as you have seen. The Pakistani establishment has answered public discontent with bullets, blackouts, intimidation and repression, and now seeks to manufacture legitimacy through a hollow electoral exercise,” he said.
Pakistan “must be held accountable” and the world “should see through the veneer of Pakistan’s hypocritical lecturing on human rights”, Jaiswal said. “The international community must hold Pakistan accountable for these atrocities.”
PoK has been affected by violence since the Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC), a local organisation, launched a protest earlier this year against high inflation and cost of living in the region. It also demanded the abolition of seats reserved in the local assembly for refugees from the Indian region of Jammu and Kashmir, which experts have contended are used by Pakistan’s security establishment to manipulate the outcome of elections.
Elections to the assembly in PoK are being held in three phases, and the first and second phases on July 27 and August 2 were marred by firing by security forces on protesters and allegations of rigging. Elections could not be held in the two constituencies that voted on Tuesday because of landslides and bad weather on Sunday. The third phase will be held on August 10.
The Pakistan People’s Party (PPP), which is part of the PML-N-led ruling coalition in Islamabad, on Tuesday accused its political partner of rigging, violence and electoral malpractices during the second phase of polling.

The CM’s remarks came after the second day of the UP assembly’s Monsoon Session saw disruptions over the Ram Temple donation theft matter. The Opposition demanded a discussion on the issue, leading to a confrontation between SP and BJP legislators. Amid the uproar, Speaker Satish Mahana adjourned the House till 11 am Wednesday and suspended SP MLA Sachin Yadav for the remainder of the session.
Addressing reporters in the assembly premises after the adjournment, Adityanath said the state government had acted promptly after the alleged theft came to light by constituting an SIT, following which eight accused were arrested.

Targeting the Opposition, Adityanath said the SP had consistently opposed the Ram Temple movement. He claimed that SP leaders did not attend the consecration ceremony in January 2024 despite receiving invitations.
“These are the same people who opposed the Ram Temple and insulted Lord Ram and the Ram Janmabhoomi movement. Today they are raising the issue only to malign the temple. Their conduct has always been against Sanatan,” he said.

headline: Supreme Court orders crackdown on digital arrest scams, faster money recovery
full_text:
Supreme Court orders crackdown on digital arrest scams, faster money recovery
A Supreme Court panel seeks tighter coordination between banks, intermediaries and police as digital arrest scams grow, with new measures aimed at blocking mule accounts and helping victims recover defrauded funds.
The Supreme Court on Tuesday issued a slew of directions to strengthen the fight against digital fraud, asking the RBI to prepare and circulate a standard operating procedure for bank accounts linked to cybercrimes and directing states and Union Territories to speed up grievance redressal and money recovery mechanisms for victims.
A bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana also asked an Inter-Departmental Committee set up by the Centre to consult banks and financial intermediaries on ways to prevent "digital arrest" scams and help victims recover defrauded money.
The bench was hearing a suo motu matter, 'In Re: Victims of Digital Arrest Related to Forged Documents'.
RBI SOP ON CYBER FRAUD, MULE ACCOUNTS
The Supreme Court directed the Reserve Bank of India to prepare and circulate an SOP for dealing with bank accounts linked to cyber frauds, including mule accounts.
The RBI has also been asked to provide copies of the SOP to the Registrars General of all high courts, allowing the guidelines to be made available across the judiciary.
STATES, UTs TOLD TO ACT ON GRIEVANCE, MONEY RECOVERY
The court directed all states, Union Territories and law enforcement agencies to ensure the expeditious adoption and operationalisation of grievance redressal and money restoration modules developed for victims of cyber-enabled financial frauds.
States and UTs were also asked to take steps to ensure public awareness about these grievance redressal and money restoration mechanisms so that citizens know where and how to seek help after being defrauded.
The Registrars General of all high courts were directed to apprise courts about the grievance redressal and money restoration modules, ensuring that victims are made aware of the remedies available to them.
STATE-WISE, BANK-WISE FRAUD DATA SOUGHT
Seeking greater accountability in the handling of cyber fraud complaints, the Supreme Court asked the authorities to submit a report providing state-wise and bank-wise details of grievances registered and disposed of under the cyber fraud redressal mechanism.
The data is expected to provide a clearer picture of how complaints are being handled across states and banking institutions.
FASTER DISPOSAL OF FROZEN BANK ACCOUNTS
The bench also directed authorities to take steps to ensure the expeditious disposal of matters relating to the freezing of bank accounts in cases involving cyber fraud investigations.
The direction comes amid the wider push to make the response to cyber-enabled financial crimes faster and more effective, particularly when money has already moved through banking channels.
PANEL TO CONSULT BANKS ON 'DIGITAL ARREST' SCAMS
The Supreme Court also asked the Inter-Departmental Committee constituted by the Centre to consult banks and financial intermediaries on measures to prevent "digital arrest" scams.
The committee has also been asked to explore ways to facilitate the recovery of money defrauded from victims.
The directions come a week after the apex court suggested that the Centre consider formally defining "digital arrest" in criminal law and treating it as a standalone offence carrying stringent punishment.
The latest directions seek to bring regulators, banks, financial intermediaries, state authorities, law enforcement agencies and the judiciary into a more coordinated framework to tackle digital fraud and improve the recovery of money lost by victims.

Air India Phuket-Delhi flight drops 300 feet after turbulence, 10 passengers, 4 crew members injured
The Air India aircraft on Tuesday experienced a sudden drop in its altitude, likely caused due to turbulence.
Fourteen passengers on board a Phuket-Delhi Air India flight were injured after it dropped about 300 feet due to turbulence before landing safely.
People aware of the matter said that Delhi airport was alerted, and medical teams were put on standby ahead of the landing. The Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA), the regulator, has been informed about the incident. “All the injured have been taken to Medanta Hospital in Gurugram and India Spinal Injury Centre," said an official requesting anonymity.

The airline said the flight AI2379 experienced a brief in-flight turbulence-related event during cruise, resulting in a momentary change in altitude. "The aircraft landed safely in Delhi, and all passengers and crew have safely disembarked.”
Air India said there were no serious injuries as of now. "A small number of passengers and crew members with minor injuries requiring medical assessment have been taken to a medical facility at the airport for precautionary examination and care by Air India’s airport team and medical personnel.”
Also Read | Airlines report 352 major flight defects till June, Akasa and Air India top list
A DGCA official, on condition of anonymity, said the pilot in command reported a severe injury to one cabin crew member, injuries to a few passengers due to a sudden loss of approximately 300 feet of altitude. The official said a transient technical fault is also suspected.
Air India said the safety and well-being of its passengers and crew remain the airline's highest priority. "We are providing all necessary support to those affected and are cooperating fully with the relevant authorities as part of the investigation,” the airline said in a statement.
The flight took off from Phuket at 8:25 am and landed in Delhi at 11:00 am, according to data on flightradar24.com.
The aircraft landed safely at Delhi's Indira Gandhi International Airport where all passengers and crew disembarked safely, Air India said, adding that no serious injuries were reported.

headline: Meta's global team in India tomorrow: Govt amid row over PM Modi's reel removal

Meta's global team in India tomorrow: Govt amid row over PM Modi's reel removal
Govt summons Meta global team in India on August 5-6, says IT Secretary S Krishnan.
The government on Tuesday said it will raise a number of issues, including lapses in tackling of CSAM (Child Sexual Exploitative and Abuse Material), as well as wrongful action on prominent account during the upcoming meeting with Meta's global team.
IT Secretary S Krishnan said that a company at the forefront of technology should have been able to make its systems work as they are supposed to.
Meta's global team will be in India on August 5 and 6, Krishnan added.
It was not immediately clear who will be part of the team that will travel to India. There have been demands by the ruling party BJP's leaders for a personal apology by CEO Mark Zuckerberg.
What led to the summoning?
This comes after Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s Facebook reel addressing India's youth and promising stringent action against paper leaks, was briefly restricted on the platform.
The ministry further said that Meta has been under regulatory scrutiny over CSAM in paid advertisements on Instagram. The government had earlier slapped a notice on Meta over the issue, news agency PTI reported.
"There are a range of issues...the CSAM issue was raised, so what measures have been taken regarding that, and synthetically generated information ... to what extent that is being looked at. Then, of course, for prominent personalities, when they have verified accounts, if content has to be taken down, there have to be safeguards...all of these will be the issues," Krishnan told reporters on the sidelines of the launch of an independent multimodal AI evaluation platform by AI4Bharat at IIT Madras and Josh Talks AI.
"We would like to understand from them (Meta) as to why some of these things have not been working the way they are supposed to work, and what are the challenges," Krishnan added.
‘Zuckerberg should apologise or…’
The chairman of the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Communications and Information Technology, Nishikant Dubey, on Monday said Meta chief executive Mark Zuckerberg should apologise for the temporary removal of PM Modi’s Facebook reel, warning that the company could otherwise lose the “safe harbour” protection available to intermediaries under Section 79 of the Information Technology (IT) Act.
“Meta’s mindset is to destabilise the country. PM Modi’s video was taken down from 12.30 am to 5 am. This is a very serious issue. Our committee has said two things — the apology must come from Mark Zuckerberg or else we will take back the safe harbour given to Meta under Section 79,” Dubey told reporters.
‘Algorithmic error’: Meta
Responding to the criticism, Meta apologised, attributing the removal to an algorithmic error, an MP said.
“An executive of Meta apologised for taking down PM Modi’s video from Facebook. He said there was some algorithm mistake. He also assured next time it won’t be repeated and that Meta will amend their algorithm,” one MP said.
Meta did not respond to HT’s request for comment.
